**Context:** Multi-phase refactoring of BudgetPro (leaddrive-budgeting) from AAC-specific prototype → multi-tenant SaaS.

---

## Summary of current issues (audit conducted 2026-04-21)

Main pain points that drive the roadmap:
- `BudgetLine.category` / `department` fields have fuzzy semantics — imports put code in one, name in the other, with no contract. Led to `looksLikeSapCode` regex fallbacks in analytics/pnl.
- `ChartOfAccount` exists but BudgetLine/COGSBudgetLine/BalanceSheetLine hold `accountCode: String` — no FK, data is denormalized.
- `import-excel/route.ts` is a 900+ line procedural monolith with no transaction, no partial re-import, no user-facing error reporting.
- `budgeting/page.tsx` is a 5000+ line god-component mixing all tabs.
- AAC-specific hardcoded product codes (`PRODUCT_CODES = ["MHB", "LIME_BURNT", ...]`) and Azerbaijani strings (`"Vahid maya dəyəri"`, `"Xammal xərcləri"`) scattered throughout.
- Pre-existing TypeScript errors ignored (`department-access.ts` missing module, `cost-model-map.ts` unknown type).
- No audit log, no soft-delete, no period locking — not compliance-ready.
- Security: weak dev admin password, org isolation done manually per endpoint (no RLS), no rate limits on import.

## Phase 1: Stabilization (2 weeks, ~50h)

**Goal:** make current imports reliable, errors visible to users, clean TypeScript.

### 1.1 Transaction-wrapped import
- ✅ Wrap `import-excel/route.ts` in `prisma.$transaction([...])`
- ✅ Split into chunks with savepoints every 5000 rows (Turn CXXIII, 2026-05-11; new `src/lib/db/chunked-create-many.ts` reusable helper with PostgreSQL SAVEPOINTs per chunk + small-payload fast path skipping savepoint overhead when `data.length ≤ chunkSize`. Applied to 5 createMany call sites in `import-excel/route.ts`: budgetLines / salesBudgetLines / balanceSheetLines / cogsBudgetLines / cogsCostDetails. 12 unit tests cover empty/below-chunkSize/above-chunkSize/custom-size/throw-rollback/skipDuplicates passthrough/savepoint-injection-guard.)
- ✅ On failure: full rollback, no half-imported state

### 1.2 Error reporting in UI
- ✅ Return `ImportResult { imported, skipped, errors: ImportError[] }`
- ✅ Log every skip with `{ sheet, row, reason, rawValue }` (P&L, BS, Assumptions — 4 key spots; extend to others on demand)
- ✅ UI: expandable error list after import
- ✅ Toast notification — **superseded 2026-05-17 Session 9**: expandable error list already covers the same UX surface. Toast was an alternative-form variant, not additional functionality. No code delta needed.

### 1.3 Fix TypeScript errors
- ✅ `src/lib/budgeting/department-access.ts` — missing `@/lib/permissions` module (created as re-export)
- ✅ `src/lib/budgeting/cost-model-map.ts` — unknown/number types (defensive `num()` helper)
- ✅ `src/lib/budgeting/report-engine.ts:370` — undefined indexing (guard with `?? ""`)
- ✅ `src/app/api/budgeting/import-excel/route.ts` — Buffer type (cast to ExcelJS.Buffer)
- ✅ Set `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors: false` in `next.config.ts`
- ✅ Add `tsc --noEmit` to pre-commit hook (Turn CXXII, 2026-05-11; in `.githooks/pre-commit` with `.ts/.tsx` diff-filter — skips on doc-only commits to keep cost predictable; ~3-5s warm cache, ~10-15s cold; bypass via `git commit --no-verify`). CI workflow integration still pending (Phase 0.7 remote setup).

### 1.4 Soft-delete + undo for reset
- ✅ Add `deletedAt: DateTime?` (+ `deletedBy`) to `BudgetPlan` — cascading via the parent covers the user-facing scope without touching 4 tables
- ✅ Replace all `deleteMany` with `updateMany({ deletedAt: now() })` (bulk reset + single-plan delete)
- ✅ Filter `deletedAt: null` in read queries (list + detail; other plan-scoped endpoints rely on plan not appearing in the list)
- ✅ "Restore" button (Recently Deleted section with 30-day countdown)
- ✅ Cron job: physical delete after 30 days (Phase 1.4 closed 2026-05-26 — Phase 6.1 BullMQ unblocked it; daily 03:00 UTC purge across BudgetPlan/CashFlowEntry/BalanceSheetLine/Counterparty via [cleanup-processor.ts](src/lib/queue/processors/cleanup-processor.ts) + `scheduleCleanupCron()`; emits one `soft_delete_purge` audit event per run with per-table counts + duration; CLEANUP_CRON env override for ops tuning)

**Goal:** eliminate code↔name confusion, denormalization, magic strings.

FK onDelete: SetNull → Restrict (admin can no longer accidentally orphan ledger rows). - ✅ Delete `PRODUCT_CODES = ["MHB", "LIME_BURNT", ...]` from code — `src/lib/import/aac-products.ts` deleted along with its sole consumer `src/app/api/budgeting/import-excel/route.ts` and the `BudgetExcelImport` UI component. AZMADE/AAC data was already removed from the DB (only AZSEKER root + 7 op-cos remain); the AAC-specific xlsx-shape importer was dead weight.
- ✅ User maps sheets → products in UI during import — superseded by Phase 7.M Tier 7 AI Auto Import (`/budgeting/admin/ai-import`) which handles any xlsx shape via LLM classifier across 14 dataTypes (PL/BS/CF/KPI/CAPEX/SALES/LAND/DESCRIPTIONS/INFO/COMPANIES/OPS_FACTS/BUDGET_ACTUALS/SALES_FORECAST + UNKNOWN). Original plan assumed per-tenant hardcoded product catalogs; AI classifier obsoletes that requirement.
- ✅ Persist mapping in `Organization.importConfig.products[]` — N/A under new model. AI Mapper caches per-sheet proposals in `AIMapperProposalCache` keyed by sheet structure (sha256), so same-template re-uploads cost $0. Per-org persistent product catalog would re-introduce the AAC-specific magic-string class of bug Tier 7 fixed.

### 2.4 Import = staging + validation + apply
**Note (CXXXII reality-check):** original 5-bullet plan was implemented via
the AI-Mapper-driven Phase 7.B onboarding wizard pipeline. Mapping:
- ✅ New `import_staging` table — shipped as Prisma model `ImportStaging` (Phase 7.B): `proposal Json` (AI mapper output) + `userOverrides Json?` (user edits) + `xlsxTempPath String?` (re-runnable) + `status enum (pending|applied|discarded|expired)` + audit fields (`createdBy` / `createdAt` / `expiresAt` / `appliedAt` / `errorMessage`).
- ✅ `/api/import/parse` endpoint → stages data — shipped as `/api/onboarding/import/analyze` (single-sheet) + `/api/onboarding/import/analyze-multi` (multi-sheet, Turn CIX) which create `ImportStaging` rows.
- ✅ UI preview + validation warnings before commit — shipped via `OnboardingWizardSwitcher` + `ImportWizardMulti` per-sheet success/error chips + AI Mapper anomaly flags (-200% margin, missing column types, etc.).
- ✅ User confirms → `/api/import/apply` → copy to production tables — shipped via `/api/onboarding/import/budget` POST (single-sheet known-shape) + apply pattern from staging row's `proposal` + `userOverrides`.
- ✅ Persist `ImportRun` history — **closed 2026-05-17 Session 9**: lifecycle fully covered via `ImportStaging` audit fields (status / createdBy / createdAt / appliedAt / errorMessage). Separate dedicated `ImportRun` model would duplicate the same semantics; not shipping a parallel model is the correct architectural call, not a gap.

## Phase 4: Audit log & compliance (2 weeks, ~80h)

**Goal:** financial audit readiness (SOX / GAAP).

### 4.1 Immutable change history
- ✅ Table `audit_events` (Prisma model `AuditEvent`, shipped Phase 7.F Turn 11): `id, organizationId, actorUserId, action (enum AuditAction), entityType, entityId, metadata (Json), context (Json?), createdAt`. 365-day retention documented in schema; auto-prune deferred to Phase 6 BullMQ.
- ✅ Typed call-site logging via `logAuditEvent(prisma, event)` at `src/lib/audit/log.ts` — discriminated-union event types (one variant per `AuditAction` enum member) lock metadata shape at compile time. **Deliberate non-middleware design** per docstring: middleware would require free-form JSON (no compile-time guarantees) + can't capture business-context semantics that vary per route. 16+ call sites integrated across mutation routes (period locks, approval requests, organization settings, intel refresh, indicator explanations, ChartOfAccount role overrides). Never-throws contract: audit-write failure returns `{ok: false, error}` so caller can surface as soft warning without breaking the calling action.
- ✅ Never-delete contract: `src/lib/audit/` exposes only `logAuditEvent` (write) + `listAuditEvents` (read) + `import-helpers` (write) + `compact-summary` (read). No DELETE/UPDATE methods anywhere; `prisma.auditEvent.delete*` not called from any module.

### 4.2 Period locking
- ✅ **DONE — Phase 4.2 closed Turn LXX.** 24 mutation handlers reject with 423 + admin UI + lock/unlock API + audit-trail on add/remove + audit-trail on 423 attempts. Foundations (LXVII) → fan-out (LXVIII) → bulk-paths (LXIX) → admin/audit (LXX). The remaining ⬜ items (indicator UI lock-icon badges in tabs) are cosmetic surface — file as Turn LXXI follow-up if user wants the visual polish, but the **CFO-protection contract is fully shipped**.
- ✅ History (sub-checklist preserved for narrative trace):
  - ✅ Add `Organization.lockedPeriods Json @default("[]")` (Turn LXVII; shape: `Array<{period, lockedAt, lockedBy, reason?}>`; period format matches `parsePeriod` — "YYYY"/"YYYY-Q[1-4]"/"YYYY-MM"; migration `20260508*_phase7g_turnlxvii_organization_locked_periods` applied)
  - ✅ NEW `src/lib/budgeting/period-lock.ts` (~150 LOC) + `src/lib/budgeting/period-lock-http.ts` (~75 LOC) — pure module: `parseLockedPeriods`/`isPeriodLockedInList`/`findLockForPeriod`/`addPeriodLock`/`removePeriodLock`/`getActivePeriodLock`/`derivePeriodKey`/`findFirstActiveLockInPeriods`; HTTP module: `lockedResponse`/`containingPeriodKeys`/`containingPeriodKeysForMonths`. 45 unit tests across both modules.
  - ✅ API rejects writes to locked periods — **24 mutation handlers** total return RFC 4918 `423 Locked` with lock metadata. Row-level CRUD (Turns LXVII + LXVIII): `lines POST/PUT/DELETE` + `actuals POST/PUT/DELETE` + `sections POST/PUT/DELETE` + `forecast POST` (multi-plan atomic) + `cogs POST` (single + bulk) + `cash-flow POST` (year/quarter/month) + `cash-flow/generate POST` (year-level + per-plan, lock-before-deleteMany). Bulk-mutation paths (Turn LXIX): `import-csv POST` (plan period) + `import-excel POST` (year + all 12 months, lock-before-$transaction) + `sync-actuals POST` (plan + current month) + `snapshot-actuals POST` (each plan + targetMonth containers, lock-before-costModelSnapshot.upsert) + `rolling POST` (12-month forward span) + `rolling PATCH` (target month containers) + `rolling/auto-forecast POST` (plan + each forecast month). Plan-level destructive/cloning ops (Turn LXIX architect Round-1 ⚠️ closure): `plans/[id]/purge DELETE` (12-table cascade) + `plans/[id]/apply-templates POST` + `plans/[id]/create-version POST` + `matrix-seed POST` (Cartesian + OpEx in $transaction). All inline 423 envelopes consolidated to shared `period-lock-http.lockedResponse()`. 60+ handler tests cover the gates including lock-before-destructive-op ordering.

  - ✅ Audit-log entry recorded on 423 fires (Turn LXX) — `lockedResponse(lock, auditCtx?)` accepts opt-in audit context; all 24 mutation routes migrated to pass `{prisma, orgId, userId, route}`. Fire-and-forget audit emission — never blocks 423. New `period_lock_blocked_mutation` audit action variant + `period_lock_add` + `period_lock_remove`. Prisma migration `phase7g_turnlxx_period_lock_audit_actions` extends `AuditAction` enum.
  - ✅ Indicator UI badge (Turn LXXIV): NEW `<PeriodLockBadge plan={...}>` component + `useActivePeriodLockForPlan` hook + i18n EN/RU/AZ. Mounted in `budgeting/page.tsx` header next to plan selector. Renders nothing when no lock active (no layout shift); shows amber lock-badge + period mono + tooltip (reason / lockedBy / lockedAt) when active plan's period is in org's lock list. 10 new tests (5 hook + 5 badge). Per-row "locked" status in tables defer to next-slice (low priority — single header badge surfaces the state cleanly for v1).

### 4.3 Approval workflow
- ✅ Phase 4.3 closed Phase 7.G Turn LXXIII (backend Turn LXXI + admin UI Turn LXXII + email notifications Turn LXXIII):
  - ✅ Table `ApprovalRequest` (Turn LXXI; migration `phase7g_turnlxxi_approval_request`). 2 enums (`ApprovalRequestStatus` pending/approved/rejected/cancelled, `ApprovalRequestType` 7 variants: budget_line/actual create/update/delete + period_unlock). Polymorphic `proposedChange Json` field — shape varies per type, validated runtime via `isValidProposedChange`.
  - ✅ NEW `src/lib/budgeting/approval-request.ts` (~250 LOC) — state-machine helpers (`canTransition`/`nextStatus`/`isTerminalStatus`) + 7 typed `proposedChange` shapes + `isValidProposedChange` runtime guard + Turn LXXII `consumeApprovalRequest` (mutation-route bypass guard with cross-user safety) + `markApprovalRequestApplied` (one-shot stamp). 22 unit tests.

Other request types (line/actual create/update/delete) approve+set appliedAt but defer apply to mutation route via `?approvalRequestId=X` bypass (Turn LXXII shipped). 14 handler tests.
  - ✅ Mutation routes accept `?approvalRequestId=X` to bypass 403/423 when an approved request matches (Turn LXXII): wired on `lines POST/PUT/DELETE` + `actuals POST/PUT/DELETE` (6 handlers). Bypass requires status=approved + matching requestType + matching targetId (for update/delete) + `requestedBy === current userId` (cross-user safe, prevents "user A approves, user B sneaks in") + appliedAt=null (one-shot). On successful mutation, `appliedAt` is stamped fire-and-forget. 3 new handler tests cover happy bypass + cross-user refused + DELETE bypass.

Wired in `/approval-requests` POST (after create) + `/approval-requests/[id]` PATCH (after approve/reject; cancel intentionally silent). Both calls fire-and-forget — email failures never reverse the underlying state change. 21 new tests cover send + recipient query + locale matrix + fallback paths. **Real-provider wire-up (SMTP/SendGrid/Resend) is a 1-line edit in `getEmailService()` once provider is chosen** — interface + factory pattern decouples the routes.

## Phase 6: Scale & performance (2-3 weeks, ~80h)

**Goal:** support 50+ clients × 100K+ rows.

### 6.1 Background jobs
- ✅ BullMQ + Redis for imports — **shipped 2026-05-21** (Phase 6 PR #14). Feature-flagged behind `QUEUE_BACKEND=bullmq`. Stack: `src/lib/queue/{redis-client,queues,worker-factory,feature-flag,job-types}.ts` + processors + `scripts/run-worker.ts` daemon. Activation: `brew services start redis` (already done) + worker daemon + env flag.
- ✅ WebSocket/SSE for import progress in UI — SSE endpoint `GET /api/queue/jobs/[id]/progress` + `useJobProgress` React hook + Queue Admin UI at `/budgeting/admin/queue` (PR #14).
- ✅ Retry policy — 3× exponential backoff (5/10/20s), DLQ retention 30 days / 5000 jobs (PR #14).

### 6.2 Analytics caching
- ⬜ Materialized views or Redis cache for byCategory / byDepartment — **deferred (evaluated 2026-06-16 + 2026-06-29).** A cache over financial aggregates re-introduces the stale-number trust risk Phase 8 exists to eliminate; needs bulletproof write-invalidation before it's safe, and is premature at 8/60 operational cos. Instead the hot reads were made cheaper *without* a cache (see 6.3) — analytics 81.6→54.8ms (2026-06-16) and the P&L route dropped 2 dead per-request queries + narrowed its budgetLine read (2026-06-29). Re-open when measured read latency at scale justifies the invalidation complexity.
- ⬜ Invalidate on write — N/A until a cache lands (see above).

### 6.3 Partitioning
- ⬜ Partition `budget_lines`, `journal_entries` by orgId or year — **deferred (premature).** No slow queries exist to justify a partitioning migration at current volume (15k budget_lines; EXPLAIN shows index scans in single-digit ms). Re-open at the 100K+-rows / 60-co target.
- ✅ Review slow queries, add/tune indexes — **DONE (evidence-driven, 2026-06-16 + 2026-06-29).** Profiled the hot paths on the live dev DB: every hot WHERE/orderBy is already covered by an index (analytics budgetLine ~2.7ms, matrix IVs ~6.2ms) — **no missing indexes**. Query-review fixes shipped: (a) `/api/budgeting/analytics` wide `include`→column `select` (81.6→54.8ms); (b) `/api/budgeting/pnl` removed two dead per-request queries (`salesBudgetLine` + `cOGSBudgetLine` with `productLine` joins — fetched, never read) and narrowed its `budgetLine` read from `SELECT *`+relation to a 6-column `select` (tsc-completeness-guarded). Partitioning is the only remaining 6.3 item and is deferred above.

### 6.4 CDN + static
- ✅ Next.js Image optimization — **N/A (no surface).** The terminal is SVG/data-viz only — `0` raw `<img>` tags in `src` (verified 2026-06-29), so there are no raster images to route through `next/image`. Re-open if image assets are ever introduced.
- ⬜ Static assets → Cloudflare R2 / S3 — **deferred (external-infra-gated).** Needs a CDN/object-store procurement decision; not a code task. Re-open on cloud-deploy procurement.

## ★ Phase 7: Enterprise Holding Risk Terminal (ACTIVE — chosen 2026-04-23)

**Goal:** Transform BudgetPro into an **Enterprise Holding Risk Terminal** for a diversified holding with ~60 operational companies across ~10 sectors. User picks Company × Indicator → sees value with threshold, sparkline, recommended-action hint. Plus holding-level heat map, scenario stress-tests, composite alerts, AI morning brief. Scope "от валюты до войны" — FX, commodity, operational, geopolitical, macro, regulatory.

**Model reference:** hybrid of **Resilinc + MetricStream workflow + Bloomberg UX layer**, adapted for emerging-market operating holdings. Not a trading terminal — no market quotes, execution, or IB chat.

**Status:** active per 2026-04-23 decision. Supersedes the prior "sellable to 2nd client" MVP path (see § below). Execution-ready plan: `.claude/plans/dreamy-leaping-manatee.md`.

### 7.A — Foundation (3 weeks) — ✅ all 4 bullets shipped (per CLAUDE.md)

- ✅ Formula engine (`expr-eval`, sandboxed) + resolvers (reuse existing FX helpers in `src/lib/budgeting/currency.ts`) — engine + 5 resolvers registered (`booking`, `company.settings`, `operationalFact`, `currencyRate`, `budgetLine`).
- ✅ Core API routes (companies, indicators, alerts) — companies, indicators, indicators/matrix, scenarios, alerts (incl. `/alerts/events` v3 read API).
- ✅ Backfill existing AAC data under Company records — 13 seeded today (8 operational); CLI importer for AZMADE budgets with transactional replace + auto-recompute.

### 7.D — Bloomberg-style UX (3 weeks) — ✅ all 6 bullets shipped
- ✅ Dark theme + JetBrains Mono monospace for numbers — wired in `src/app/globals.css` + Risk Terminal at `/budgeting/terminal` page; HeroSection / CompositeTrendChart use mono numerics.
- ✅ Command bar + function-code parser (`HILTN FX GO`, `HOLD HEAT GO`) — `src/features/terminal/components/CommandBar.tsx` with locale-aware tests. Token parser → dispatch wiring per-function.
- ✅ Multi-pane workspace (2×2 default, drag-resize, saveable named layouts) — `PanelGrid.tsx` + `LayoutMenu.tsx` (saveable layouts persisted server-side).
- ✅ Keyboard-first (`Ctrl+K` focus cmd bar, panel cycling, F-key workspaces, `/` in-panel search) — `HotkeyToolbar.tsx` + `KeyboardShortcutsModal.tsx`.
- ✅ Functions: `HOLD`, `GRP`, `CO`, `IND`, `SEC`, `CMP`, `ALT`, `SCN`, `BRF` — wired through CommandBar parser.
- ✅ **Activity-aware HeatMap disclosure (shipped 2026-07-16; hardened after production audit).** The focused-company view hides only indicators outside the selected activity profile by default; universal and applicable-but-missing indicators remain visible so data gaps are not disguised. Mixed subgroups derive activity from their descendants, unknown leaf scope fails open, and an explicit `CompanyIndicator.enabled` assignment wins for its exact company/indicator pair. A persisted coloured/unknown cell is output, never applicability evidence. The same canonical pair contract now gates the matrix, manual/batch recompute, status summary, alerts and both scenario modes before their downstream counts or aggregates. Formula structure is a higher-order constraint: a `rollup:`-bearing KPI is parent-only and cannot be enabled on an operational leaf even by an explicit assignment, which prevents zombie leaf observations and false missing-data actions. The always-visible `Hide non-applicable` toggle exposes the hidden count, reveals the full catalogue when switched off, and collapses back without changing data; count and EN/RU/AZ copy remain honest under indicator search. The old `Hide unknown` preference/control was removed so an applicable-but-empty KPI cannot be silently suppressed. Materiality remains a separate presentation signal: `not_material` cells stay visible but dimmed when their KPI is activity-applicable.

- ✅ **E2E test harness** — Playwright shipped 2026-05-03 across 3 turns (D.1 login+terminal 3 cases / D.2 onboarding wizard 4 cases / D.3 recompute+SSE 3 cases). 10/10 pass empirically against live dev server in 1.0min. Critical-path coverage: auth, dashboard render, wizard state machine, AI Data Mapper happy-path (LLM-gated), API contract, SSE LISTEN/NOTIFY end-to-end. Per-sector pack E2E is a v2 expansion (current 10 cases cover the cross-sector mechanics).
- ✅ **Admin documentation** — `docs/ADMIN_RUNBOOK.md` v1 shipped 2026-05-03 (740 LOC, 12 sections + glossary + escalation paths). Covers customer onboarding, indicator catalog management, alert tuning, recompute pipeline, historical IV backfill, audit log, top-10 troubleshooting playbook, DB ops, vocabulary glossary, file-path map.
- ✅ **Deployment readiness** — `docs/DEPLOYMENT_READINESS.md` v1 shipped 2026-05-03 (597 LOC, 9 sections). SRE/DevOps pre-prod gate audience.
- ✅ **SSE serverless ADR** — `docs/DESIGN_SSE_SERVERLESS.md` v1.1 shipped 2026-05-03 (~570 LOC, 6 options + 12-dim matrix + recommendation + 4 trigger conditions). Implementation gated on user-decision triggers.
- ⬜ User acceptance sign-off (post-customer-pilot)
- 🟡 **Production free-feed scheduler / EIA activation (local implementation verified 2026-07-17; production activation still open).** Manual refresh and `/api/cron/refresh-feeds` share one canonical credential source: `Organization.settings.apiKeys` per organization; the cron constructs a separate adapter set inside each org loop and no longer reads global EIA/USDA/GTrends env keys. The tracked VM systemd timer/runner is implemented but disabled by default: it excludes Anthropic and paid Google Trends, keeps the bearer out of argv, requires a recent successful canary before enablement, retries bounded failures, records a dedicated heartbeat, and uses a PostgreSQL advisory lock to prevent overlapping refreshes. Missing optional free-provider keys are reported as skipped configuration; a partial/degraded run returns non-2xx so neither systemd nor the canary can treat it as success. Manual refresh validates known source + required key before consuming the 1/min quota, returns structured `api_key_missing` guidance, preserves `Retry-After`, and the Drift UI surfaces both states plus zero-point provider errors. Local handler/policy/lock tests, TypeScript, shell syntax and systemd unit verification are green; the earlier signed-in local EIA proof wrote 3 points and changed `eia-energy` from missing to fresh. **Still open and not changed here:** owner-approved deploy, confirm/configure the production org EIA key, install the units without enabling them, run one explicitly approved write-capable canary, inspect its data + heartbeat, then enable and verify the scheduled production heartbeat and exact deployed SHA.

**Estimated total: ~20 weeks (~5 months) focused work.**

## MVP path (SUPERSEDED 2026-04-23 — kept for reference)

> **Superseded 2026-04-23** by Phase 7 (Enterprise Holding Risk Terminal). Rationale: real deployment is a ~60-company holding with only 1 company (AAC) currently onboarded; serving an abstract 2nd client before fully serving the real 1st one is premature. Most items here (multi-entity model, industry templates, onboarding wizard) fall out of Phase 7.A–7.B as natural byproducts — they're delivered, just re-sequenced. The i18n cleanup is the only item that may need separate scheduling if/when a second client becomes concrete.

To reach "sellable to a second client" with minimum rework, the team agreed
to skip the full Phase 2 / 3 / 4 refactors and pull the highest-leverage items
from 5 forward. Everything else stays on the roadmap for after the first
paying client signs.

### Product constraints locked in

- **English-only.** No multi-locale. Delete next-intl plumbing and hardcode
  English strings — removes a whole category of bugs and saves onboarding time.
- **Enterprise B2B, no self-serve billing.** Contracts are signed offline; we
  don't need Stripe, pricing pages, paywalls, plan gating UI, or feature flags
  driven by subscription tier. Org access is toggled manually by an admin.

### MVP scope (in order)

1. **Phase 2.3** — Remove AAC product hardcode; client maps sheets→products in UI
2. **Phase 5.1** — Configurable Chart of Accounts via `role` field (so analytics
   stops grepping SAP code prefixes like 711/721/731 and works for ANY numbering)
3. **Phase 5.3** — Onboarding wizard (Org details → CoA upload → column mapping
   → first import → done)
4. **i18n cleanup** — Rip out next-intl, inline all strings as English literals

### Skipped for MVP (revisit after first paying client)

- Phase 2.2 (non-English keyword mapping) — English-only locks this out entirely
- Phase 2.4 (staging import) — direct import works well enough
- Phase 3 (UI refactor) — 5k-line page.tsx is ugly but not blocking sales
- Phase 4 (audit log) — needed for regulated enterprise, not for MVP
- Phase 5.2 (RLS) — app-level isolation is audited in Phase 0.2
- Phase 5.4 (billing) — **permanently** skipped; B2B contracts, not SaaS self-serve
- Phase 6 (scale) — 50+ clients is a future problem

Estimated: **~6-8 weeks of focused work** to MVP (slightly less now that
billing and i18n plumbing are out of scope).

Triaged by buildability. **#5 ✅ built 2026-06-01** (see changelog); #1–#4 still need a design pass before implementation.

1. ✅ **Per-hectare benchmark bands (DONE 2026-06-01 — v1)** — the agro per-ha indicators (`AGRO_REVENUE_PER_HA`, `AGRO_COST_PER_HA`, `AGRO_YIELD_PER_HA`, `AGRO_YIELD_EFFICIENCY`) show a value but no benchmark. Client: "show the floor (aşağı planka) AND the best-case ceiling (yuxarı planka) per ha so I can tell if my number is good." → Surface the indicator `thresholds` as an explicit benchmark range in IndicatorDetail + a real per-crop/region best-case figure. Effort: **M** (threshold display is quick; the best-case number needs an agro-benchmark data source).
2. **Post-import IFRS-conformance check** — "FS IFRS uyğun yığılmasını yoxlamaq, importdan sonra" = after import, validate the financial statements conform to IFRS. → New validation pass (extend `scripts/audit-company.cjs` or a new IFRS-structure checker: COGS≠OPEX separation, D&A its own line, BS balances, statement linkage). Effort: **M-L**.
3. **Regional peer comparison** — compare the entity vs same-industry companies in regional countries (TR/RU/GE/IR). → Extend the existing `PeerPanel` / `PeerBenchmarkModal` / `ComparePanel` (today they compare INTERNAL holding cos) with an external regional-peer dataset. Effort: **L + DATA-BLOCKED** (needs a peer-company financials source).
4. **Imported-input tagging for FX simulation** — identify what is purchased externally (foreign currency) so the currency What-if can rank which cost lines / products suffer most on a devaluation. → Per-COGS-line (or per-input) import-share + currency tag → FX What-if per-line impact ranking. Ties to `FX_IMPORTED_INPUT` + `fxExposureSource`. Effort: **M-L** + needs per-input import-share data.
5. ✅ **Fuzzy / semantic indicator search in Panel 2 (HeatMap)** — "many indicators; I had to hover one-by-one to find the per-ha one — need a search that understands intent even on an inexact word." → **DONE 2026-06-01.** New `find indicator…` input in the HeatMap toolbar (beside the company-row `/`-filter) fuzzy-filters the matrix COLUMNS. Matcher `src/features/terminal/lib/indicator-search.ts` is multilingual (matches `code` + `nameEn`/`nameRu`/`nameAz`, so typing in EN/RU/AZ finds it regardless of UI locale) and inexact-tolerant (exact → prefix → reverse-prefix for declension «гектар»↔«гектару» → substring → char-drift typos). 18 tests (13 matcher unit + 5 happy-dom UI integration).

## Phase 8: Honesty & Real-Data Workflow (NEW 2026-05-27, post-audit)

After 2026-05-27 internal audit revealed AI-fabricated data was being shown alongside real client data without distinction, this phase establishes the workflow + UI surfaces that make data provenance explicit. **Driver:** financial users cannot tolerate AI-invented risk indicators — every data point shown must be traceable to real source.

### Group A — Honesty layer (high priority, 1–2 weeks)
- ✅ **A1.** UI badge «⚠️ Pending client verification» on entity Risk Registry cards without data — shipped 2026-05-28. Strategic-context API now returns a `riskRegistry: { itemCount, source, importedAt, pendingVerification }` block for every level-2 operational entity; CompanyStrategicContextCard renders a rose-bordered «Pending client verification» banner for the 5 entities without KRI data (AZSF/CPC/MALT/FARM/HORIZON/PROMALT) and an emerald «N KRI занесены» chip for EDEN (15 real KRIs from `Top risk - EDEN AGRO MMC.xlsx`). 4 handler tests + 3 UI tests cover null (level-1), pending, populated paths.

Cell d/e/m letter at top-left (existing), ProvenanceBadge in IndicatorDetail (existing), and a colour-coded pill in HeatMap tooltip (this turn) — emerald for disclosed, amber for macro/modeled_industry, rose for modeled_generic. Visual contract identical across surfaces.
- ✅ **A3.** "Hide unknown" toggle shipped 2026-05-27 (commit `f64c89c`) and was retired 2026-07-16. Applicable-but-empty KPIs now remain visible as honest data gaps; the separate activity filter hides only non-applicable indicators.
- ✅ **A4.** Data-freshness — COMPLETE 2026-05-29. Org-wide badge shipped 2026-05-27 (matrix `lastComputedAt = MAX(IndicatorValue.computedAt)` → HeatMap header `<FreshnessLabel>`). **Per-company chip in CompanyTree row now shipped (the deferred v2):** the cell `computedAt` (already emitted by the matrix route for the org-wide aggregate) is now typed on `HeatMapCell`; CompanyTree derives `freshnessByCode` via a client-side MAX-by-companyId groupby of `matrix.cells`, with sub-groups inheriting MAX(own, descendants) through the same parent-walk as `compositeByCode` (zero extra fetch — reuses the module-cached matrix). New `RowFreshness` chip renders a fixed-width (`w-9`) emerald/amber dot + compact age ("2h"/"15m"/"3d"/"now"), `data-volatile` so the visual gate masks the ticking text. Shared `formatFreshness` util (`terminal/lib/relative-time.ts`) is the single source for both the header label and the chip — `FreshnessLabel` refactored onto it (output byte-identical). **Visual gate:** terminal-heatmap baseline regenerated — diff was the chip + masking two pre-existing unmasked volatile elements (`[you ✨]` per-user usage chip + the MarketTicker strip) that had been silently drifting the baseline (confirmed via `git stash`: clean code already failed ~1488px); both now `data-volatile`, gate green + stable. 7 formatter unit tests + 4 CompanyTree chip tests (fresh/stale/no-data/MAX-of-multiple). tsc 0 + full vitest 5367 green. **Group A fully closed.**

### Group F — Operations
- ✅ **F1.** Catalog audit + scope-to-active-industries — DONE 2026-05-29. **Audit finding:** the *compute* path was already correctly multi-org-scoped — `matchCompaniesToIndicators` (`targets.ts`) only pairs a company with a def when `def.industries.length === 0 || def.industries.includes(company.industry)`, so the ~77 other-industry defs (hospitality/pharma/construction/…) never produced IVs for AZSEKER and never reached the HeatMap. The "110 vs 33" was **by-design multi-tenant catalog**, not a bug; a global `isActive=false` on the irrelevant defs would have been WRONG (it'd hide them from a future hospitality/pharma org). **What was actually cluttered:** the catalog *list* endpoint `GET /api/indicators` returned all 110 to its consumers (AlertRulesEditor, HotkeyToolbar) regardless of the org's sectors. **Fix (query-time, multi-org-safe):** GET now derives the org's active industries from its companies (`company.findMany distinct industry`) and filters the catalog to `industries isEmpty OR hasSome(orgIndustries)` — universal indicators always pass; a fresh org with no companies sees universal-only and widens as it onboards. No schema change, no compute change, no HeatMap change. +1 handler test. tsc 0 • full vitest 5356 green.
- ✅ **F2.** /guide telemetry — shipped 2026-05-28 as first-party (no external dep). New `GuideView` Prisma model + `POST /api/telemetry/guide-view` beacon. GuideViewer fires the beacon on initial mount (anchor=null) + on every IntersectionObserver active-slug change (500ms debounce); uses `navigator.sendBeacon` with `fetch keepalive` fallback so tab-close / unload don't lose the last view. Anonymous sessions log with `organizationId=null, actorUserId=null`; authenticated sessions stamp both. IP rate-limit 10/min. PII-light: User-Agent truncated to 200 chars; no fingerprinting. 6 handler tests. Reads via direct Prisma queries from future admin /guide-stats page (deferred to v2 — bare table is enough for ad-hoc SQL inspection today).
- ✅ **F3.** CARRYOVER weekly SLA scanner — shipped 2026-05-28. Pure helper `src/lib/carryover/scan-stale-rows.ts` parses `docs/CARRYOVER.md`, extracts the `## OPEN` section, returns rows past a configurable cutoff (default 30d), and tags `owner=user` separately as the highest-leverage escalation tier. CLI script `npm run carryover:sla` (or `npx tsx scripts/carryover-sla-scan.ts`) prints a stdout summary and exits 1 when stale rows are present so cron / LaunchAgent wrappers can fire a notification. Tested live: 5 OPEN rows, 1 stale (30d, owner=user). 11 unit tests + 0 deps. Cron wiring left to user — see script docstring for cron.d / LaunchAgent suggestion.

## Phase 10: Risk Terminal 2.0 — Trust Core & Decision Cockpit (NEW 2026-07-15)

**Full package:** `docs/risk-terminal-2.0/` (7 documents). **Live execution record:** `docs/risk-terminal-2.0/IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md` — read that for per-slice status, evidence and open owner decisions; this section is the phase-level summary only.

Trust-first transformation of the Risk Terminal: one canonical financial path, explicit period/revision contracts, a certified KPI subset, lineage, separated Risk × Confidence × Coverage, and a decision-first UI — with the existing Expert Matrix **preserved** as a mode, not deleted. Strangler migration; **no big-bang rewrite**. Audit verdict: UI 6/10, UX 5/10, data trust 4.5/10, confusion 8.5/10 — the engine is strong, the assurance around it is not.

**Why now (evidence, not theory):** the 2026-07-15 FO-workbook session found five defects that each silently changed money on screen — subsidies subtracted from revenue (sign read off the wrong field), credit notes added to cost, a month of revenue booked to the previous year by a 24s timezone drift, kilograms rendered as tonnes, and an operating company's P&L routed to the holding. None were caught by types or unit tests; all were caught by comparing a rendered number to the source. Phase 10 makes that comparison structural.

**Operating rules (from `CLAUDE-CODE-HANDOFF.md`):** one approved slice at a time, never all stages at once; each stage gated on human review; no production deploy/migration without explicit scope; owner sign-off required for any KPI methodology or financial total. Status vocabulary is strict — `implemented` / `tested` / `visually verified` / `reconciled` / `methodology-approved` / `provisional` / `shadow-only` / `not tested` / `blocked`. **Never `done` on compilation alone.**

## Phase 11: Import round-trip integrity (NEW 2026-07-29, owner-requested audit)

**Owner question that triggered this:** «если удалить данные через AI Import и добавить заново — всё ли сядет правильно до последнего нуля, и покажет ли UI это верно?»

**Audit method:** 45-agent parallel audit over 11 dimensions (delete semantics, atomicity, sheet coverage, numeric fidelity, period mapping, entity resolution, CoA mapping, display path, control totals, orphans/cascade, real-file coverage), each top finding adversarially re-verified against source. 28 findings survived. The five blockers below were additionally verified line-by-line by the main session before being written here.

**Verdict: the round trip is NOT provably lossless today, and — more serious than any individual defect — the system cannot tell you whether it was.** The reconciliation layer that would prove it exists, is written, and is disconnected at three independent points (11.2). Everything else in this phase is a specific way a number can move, vanish or double while the screen stays green.

**Scope boundary:** this phase is about *ingestion truth* (did the workbook's numbers land exactly once, in the right row, and does the UI read them back). It is upstream of, and independent from, Phase 10's *statement truth* (do the landed numbers reconcile as financial statements). 11.2 and 11.13 are the natural feeders for 10.B1/10.B5 — an import that cannot prove its own row counts cannot supply decision-grade lineage.

### Blockers — must land before any round-trip rehearsal

|---|------|----------|------|--------|
| 11.1 | ✅ **DONE 2026-07-29** — reset scope's company dimension now derived from the inserted rows (`footprintCompanyIds`), date window left caller-controlled per the `kpi-import-batch` precedent; `assertNoCollateralDeletion` wired with an independently-written count WHERE so future drift between the two clauses is loud; `companyId: null` kept as a legitimate footprint member (org-wide actuals) with the OR-composition it needs; empty footprint degrades to `{ in: [] }` so a zero-row parse can no longer delete-without-reinsert; `defaultReadActualSums` scoped to the same footprint (otherwise the company-less recon key would fold surviving sibling rows in and report a false mismatch). 6 new tests + 2 rewritten (they pinned the old plan-wide WHERE); 11 pass, `tsc --noEmit` exit 0, 1096 onboarding/import tests green. **11.1b ✅ DONE 2026-07-29:** new `BudgetActual.source` (migration `20260729140000_budget_actual_source`) closes both halves. `NULL` = a row no import wrote — legacy, typed in through /budgeting, auto-sync, snapshot — and the reset no longer touches those, which matters because this table has no `deletedAt`. ### Status snapshot (2026-07-29, end of implementation session)

**All 14 tasks landed** across 12 commits — the 5 blockers, the 6 highs, and the 3 mediums. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 and the full suite green (7395 passed / 0 failed) at every commit.

**Migrations verified against a real database (2026-07-29).** Both were applied to a throwaway `postgres:16` with the full 29-migration chain, not just reviewed. This caught a live defect: the plan-duplicate guard referenced `organization_id` / `deleted_at`, but the columns are the quoted camelCase `"organizationId"` / `"deletedAt"` — Postgres folds unquoted identifiers to lower case, so the guard would have died with `column "organization_id" does not exist`, a misleading failure that looks like a broken migration and would have **masked the very duplicates it exists to find**. Fixed and re-verified end to end: seeding the exact split (`Azərşəkər 2026 Actuals` + `AI-Imported 2026 Budget`, both live, both `kind='actual'`) makes the migration RAISE and name both plans; soft-deleting the loser lets it apply; the index then rejects a second live actual plan, still allows a `budget` plan for the same year, and still allows a soft-deleted row to repeat the live `(year, kind)` — which is exactly why it is a partial index and not a Prisma `@@unique`. `prisma migrate diff` reports **no drift** between `schema.prisma` and the migrated database.

**Production pre-flight RUN and RESOLVED (2026-07-29).** `deploy/check-duplicate-plans.sh` (read-only, follows the `update-prod.sh` credential pattern) found the 11.4 split live on production: two plans for `(2026, actual)` — `Azərşəkər 2026 Actuals` and `June 2026`.

**Measured, not assumed — and the measurement corrected the expectation.** There was **no double-counting**: the two plans did not overlap by a single cell (Jan–May vs June only), 2026 revenue read identically with and without the second plan (₼9,531,436.67), and all 339 of its lines carried `plannedAmount = 0.00` with `companyId = NULL`. It was an **empty monthly scaffold** created through the UI on 2026-07-08 and never filled (`createdAt == updatedAt`, `periodType: monthly`). So the generic "every number doubles" description of this defect class did **not** apply to this instance.

The structural risk was still real: with two live `kind=actual` plans, each import's clean-slate is plan-scoped, so neither could ever reach the other's rows — the June layer would have been stranded permanently, and would have become genuine double-counting the moment anything was written into it.

Owner approved soft-deleting it (2026-07-29). Applied as a single guarded `UPDATE` that refuses if any non-zero line had appeared since the check; `deletedBy = 'phase-11.4-preflight'`, fully reversible by clearing `deletedAt`. Re-running the pre-flight now reports **zero split groups**, so the unique-index migration will apply on the next deploy.

**Two migrations are written but NOT yet applied to production — they run in the deploy entrypoint:**
- `20260729120000_budget_plan_unique_per_year_kind` — pre-flight now **clean**, see above. It still RAISEs if a split reappears before deploy; re-run `bash deploy/check-duplicate-plans.sh` to confirm.
- `20260729130000_import_batch_report` is additive and safe, but ships with the same deploy.

**Deliberately deferred, with reasons (not forgotten):** 11.1b (same-company multi-sheet ACTUALS clobber — needs a `source` ownership column, gated on owner questions 2–3) · 11.5b (pre-fill year from the workbook + hard-block on year mismatch) · 11.6b (`SalesForecast` has no company dimension at all — needs a schema change) · 11.7b (`sparklineComputedAt`, so freshness stops reporting a stale series as fresh) · 11.8b (`@@unique` on the financial tables — impossible until the duplicates the now-fixed races produced are cleaned) · 11.9b (two named adapters still hardcode the cost-sign flip; latent, not active).

**Answer to the owner's original question, as of now:** a delete → re-import round trip no longer loses numbers silently, and — the part that was actually missing — the system can now *tell you* whether it did. The verdict on screen is backed by a real post-write database re-read, a dropped file returns 409 instead of `ok: true`, and the evidence is persisted per run. What remains open is listed above; none of it is a silent-corruption path.

### Execution order

11.1 first and alone — it is the only irreversible data loss in the audit, and any round-trip rehearsal before it can destroy another company's actuals. Then 11.2 (nothing after it is verifiable without it; fix the reader scope in `import-batch.ts` *before* enabling the check, or every legitimate import fails), then 11.3 (11.2 catches wrong numbers, 11.3 catches missing ones — after both, the screen is worth believing). Then 11.4 (needs a migration), 11.5, 11.6, 11.7, 11.8 (unique indexes only after the data is clean), then 11.9-11.14 in any order.

### Confirmed-correct — do NOT rebuild

Recorded so this phase is not mistaken for "the import is broken". It is not; these were verified against source during the same audit:

- **`BudgetLine` / `BalanceSheetLine` / `CashFlowEntry` / `OperationalFact` replacement is correct.** Delete scope is *derived from the rows being inserted* (`footprintCompanyIds`, `planIds`), not from caller-supplied breadth — `import-batch.ts:248,260`, `bs-import-batch.ts:201-256`, `cf-import-batch.ts:300-323`, `kpi-import-batch.ts:143-180`. `assertNoCollateralDeletion` is genuinely wired at five sites and throws inside the write transaction. The 2026-05-31 and 2026-06-11 collateral-wipe classes are closed.
- **`OperationalFact` reset is inverted safely** — deletes only import provenance, structurally preserving `manual` / `manual-bulk` / `inline:*` (`archive.ts:69-74`, `:388-397`).
- **Group atomicity is real** — `$transaction(..., { maxWait: 15_000, timeout: 120_000 })`, timeout raised from a measured 5114 ms failure on Guvven Fin; all six batch helpers correctly detect and reuse an outer transaction.
- **Three pre-write gates abort before any DB write:** cross-file conflicts (`:930`, `:1212-1227`), unresolved `planKind` (`sheet-routing.ts:152` → `:611-627` → `:1168-1208`), unrecognized CoA labels (Gate A2, `:1065-1071`, `:1167-1210`, pinned by test).
- **Formula cells** — every entry point reads with `cellFormula: false`, i.e. Excel's cached values. A `Итого`/`Cəmi`/`Total` column cannot become a 13th month (closed `MONTH_INDEX` table + `continue` on miss, `applier.ts:160-168`); Total is instead used as a per-row control (`:715-733`).
- **Currency** — no implicit conversion anywhere. `currency-evidence.ts:100-119` requires a valid ISO code, a positive historical rate and source×rate agreement within 1 bp, else throws; it runs *before* the destructive phase.
- **No `misc`/`uncategorized` bucket exists** (grep-confirmed) — an unrecognized row never parks in someone else's account, so P&L subtotals never silently absorb foreign numbers. `ChartOfAccount` has `@@unique([organizationId, code])` (`prisma/schema.prisma:854`), all writers go through an atomic upsert, and no path deletes CoA rows — codes survive the round trip.
- **`monthIndex` is written explicitly and mirrored into `sortOrder`**; readers prefer `monthIndex` with a `sortOrder` fallback. The "all months collapsed into January" bug is closed.
- **Live UI refresh works end-to-end** — NOTIFY on `indicator_values` → postgres-listener → `/api/events/stream` → `use-heat-map-model.ts:227-238`, 150 ms debounce. No Next.js server cache can serve stale post-import data (no `unstable_cache`, no route-segment caching on these paths). Every surface and the recompute readers correctly exclude soft-deleted rows.
- **Zombie guard is correct and carries the DELETE side** — `recompute.ts:695-712` demotes to `status='unknown'` with machine reasons, so a correctly archived deletion greys the HeatMap rather than painting a green zero.
- **FK cascades are right** — all financial children cascade from `BudgetPlan`, and `IndicatorValue`/`CompanyIndicator`/`OperationalFact`/`Counterparty`/`ImportStaging` from `Company`. No dangling financial rows.
- **Upload sizing is unified and sufficient** — `upload-limits.ts:22` (64 MB) imported by all eight import routes, `next.config.ts:30` proxy at 96 MB. The 2026-06-21 silent truncation of the 26 MB pack is genuinely fixed; `Reporting 2026.xlsx` is importable today via `/budgeting/admin/reporting-pack` (`maxDuration: 300`).
- **All 10 real client xlsx have a NAMED adapter** — none falls through to the generic classifier. `Guvven Fin` → `azseker-plf` + `azseker-workbook-{bs,cf,kpi,capex,sales,descriptions}`; `Çıxarışların uçotu` → LAND_REGISTRY; `Açıq məhkəmə mübahisələri` → LEGAL_CASES; `Follow up - For GTC` → AUDIT_FINDINGS; `Top risk - EDEN AGRO` → risk register; `Farming strategy - Guvven` → `azseker-farming-strategy`; `Reporting 2026` → reporting-pack; **`Top 10` → `counterparty-register.ts` (file named verbatim in the source); `actual-budget-v1` → `bu-column-split.ts` ("canonical case")**.
- **`sales-product-import-batch.ts` already does verify-after-write** (`:119-153` re-reads and throws on a >0.01 mismatch, rolling back) — this is the shape 11.2 should generalize.
- **`azseker-consolidated-bs.ts:177-193` is the one in-file monetary guard that actually throws** (Σ leaves vs ASSETS/EQUITY/LIABILITIES subtotals, ±1 AZN monthly) — the pattern to replicate.

### Open questions for the owner (code cannot answer these)

1. **BS units in `Reporting 2026.xlsx`** — is that sheet really in thousands of manat? `azseker-consolidated-bs.ts:116` unconditionally multiplies every numeric cell by 1000, and the internal Σ-leaves-vs-subtotal guard is scale-invariant, so it can never catch a wrong multiplier. One screenshot of the sheet header settles it.
2. **How many `BUDGET_ACTUALS` sheets appear in one workbook, and do they span different entities?** Determines whether 11.1 is already firing today or only on the next delivery.
3. **Do hand-entered `BudgetActual` rows exist** (entered via /budgeting, not imported)? Determines whether 11.1 needs the `source` column or company scoping alone suffices.
4. **DB fact needed:** `SELECT id, name, year, kind, deleted_at FROM budget_plans WHERE organization_id = <org>` — shows whether 11.4 has already produced a duplicate plan.
5. **Are there `IndicatorValue` rows with granular periods** (`period LIKE '%-%'`)? If yes, 11.7 is mandatory; if no, granular recompute can be deferred to deletion-on-reset only.
6. **Is .docx ingestion wanted at all?** No parser exists (no `mammoth`/`docx`/`officeparser` in `package.json`; every input is `accept=".xlsx"`), so the three `AzerSheker_*.docx` files have no path. If that narrative belongs in `Company.settings.strategicDescription` it is separate work; if it keeps arriving via the `Təsvir` sheet, nothing to build.

## Phase 12: Sequential Web Security Verification (NEW 2026-07-21, renumbered from 11 on 2026-07-29)

**Standard:** `docs/security/SECURITY_AUDIT_STANDARD.ru.md`
**BudgetPro register:** `docs/security/BUDGETPRO_SECURITY_AUDIT_REGISTER.md`

Reusable evidence-first audit covering the attack classes requested by the
owner. Execution is deliberately serial: one control → one report → owner
decision → approved fix and retest → explicit permission for the next control.
Old roadmap checkmarks are treated as hypotheses until the new control produces
a repeatable negative test. No production brute force, injection, SSRF,
cross-tenant mutation, load test or restore exercise is implied by this phase.

- ✅ **12.0** Publish reusable standard, report template, BudgetPro register,
  safe-test rules, status vocabulary and owner gates.
- 🟡 **12.1 / A01** Brute-force login protection — static audit started, then paused by owner 2026-07-21 before the report/dynamic test; no fix made and A02 not started.
- ⬜ **12.2 / A02** Credential stuffing, password policy and MFA.
- 🟡 **12.3 / A03** Secret exposure — **repo swept 2026-08-02, clean; one latent issue named.** The scanner runs in BOTH pre-commit and CI, and CI uses `--scan-files` over every tracked file rather than the diff, so a secret cannot arrive via a path the hook missed. An independent grep for `sk-ant` / `AKIA` / PEM headers / Slack tokens returns only `src/lib/ai/client.test.ts` fixtures with `XXX` / `YYY` / `zzz` placeholders. **Latent, not live:** `Organization.settings.apiKeys.anthropic` is a supported source for a per-tenant Anthropic key (`/budgeting/admin/api-keys`) and there is no encryption on that path — it would sit in plaintext JSON in the database, readable by anyone with a DB dump or an admin session. Verified on production: **no org has `apiKeys` set at all**, the key comes from the deployment environment, so nothing is exposed today. Whoever first uses that admin screen creates the exposure, which makes this worth fixing before the feature is used rather than after.
- 🟡 **12.4 / A04** IDOR/BOLA object authorization — **first pass done 2026-08-02, and it corrects this repo's own standing claim.** CLAUDE.md says org isolation is "enforced at the application layer, no RLS". That is out of date: `withOrgScope` sets `app.organization_id` per transaction on an RLS-enforced client (`DATABASE_URL_APP` → role `budgetpro_app`, verified on production as neither superuser nor `bypassrls`, with tables owned by a different role so the missing `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` costs nothing). Proven live rather than read: with the tenant GUC set to the real org the app role sees 7 companies and 6,460 indicator values; set to another org, 0; unset, 0. **Two real gaps found and closed.** Of 76 public tables, 70 had RLS; `guide_views` and `import_batch_reports` carry `organizationId`, had none, and returned all 7 rows each regardless of tenant. Exposure today is nil — production has one organization — which is a fact about the DATA, not the boundary, and expires the day Phase 5 lands a second tenant; `import_batch_reports` is the one that would matter, holding import receipts that name companies, files and row counts. `company_indicators` (no tenant column, scoped through its parent, empty today) closed at the same time. **Why the existing gate missed it:** `rls-coverage-scan.mjs` checks CALL SITES — that routes wrap Prisma in `withOrgScope` — and never asks the database whether a table has a policy, so zero-policy tables pass a green build. New companion `rls-schema-coverage-scan.mjs` asserts every model with `organizationId` has `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` + a policy in the migrations; verified non-vacuous by removing the fix and watching it exit 1 on exactly those two tables. The migration was rehearsed against production inside a transaction and rolled back: wrong tenant 0 rows, own tenant 7. **Per-route review DONE later the same day, and it found a second real defect.** All 58 dynamic-id routes (excluding NextAuth) sorted into three buckets by which client they use, because that decides what has to be proved: **45** go through `withOrgScope`, so RLS filters at the database and a bare `where { id }` cannot reach another tenant's row; **6** deliberately use `prismaAdmin` — every one carries a `rls-scan-ignore:` reason, a role guard, and fetches its target with `organizationId` in the `where`, verified individually; **7** use the plain client and were read line by line. Six of those seven are sound (`recompute/jobs` scopes through a helper, `help-videos/[file]` is an anchored filename allowlist that admits no dot or slash, `recent-crossings` and `impact-forecasts` pass `session.orgId` into their helpers, `approval-requests/[id]` establishes ownership at the fetch, re-checks it in the `updateMany`, and mutates inside `withOrgScope`). **The seventh was open:** `/api/queue/jobs/[jobId]` and its SSE `/progress` sibling both read `if (data.organizationId && data.organizationId !== session.orgId)` — so a job whose payload carried no tenant was readable by any authenticated user of any organization, and the guard's correctness rested on every enqueue site remembering the field. Not academic: `recomputePair` ids are built from org/company/year and `recomputeBatch` takes Redis' sequential counter, so they are guessable, and the response carries `failedReason` (which names companies) and `result`. Now fails closed — free of cost, because both queues this route probes declare `organizationId` as REQUIRED in `job-types.ts`; the only optional-org payload is `CleanupSoftDeletedJob` on a queue neither route touches. Six tests, verified non-vacuous by restoring the old condition and watching two of them fail. **Still open on A04:** the schema gate cannot see join tables scoped through a parent, so a periodic `pg_tables` audit is owed.
- 🟡 **12.5 / A05** Function-level access control — **a write floor shipped 2026-08-02; per-endpoint role review still owed.** Measured: **42 of 117 mutating API routes call no `requireRole` at all.** That is not "unauthenticated" — `proxy.ts` already 401s every `/api/*` outside four `publicPaths`, and its per-path `RATE_RULES` are rate limits, not authorization, which is exactly what makes them easy to misread as RBAC. What it did mean is that any logged-in user could write: a `viewer` — the role whose entire purpose is read-only — could POST budget lines, PUT/DELETE saved reports and templates, seed templates, edit the chart of accounts, remove integrations and patch approval requests. Exposure today nil (production has one user, an admin), same shape as the RLS gap found the same day: a fact about the data, not about the control, and the product ships a role-management UI. **Fixed centrally rather than in 42 handlers** — one floor cannot be forgotten by the forty-third route, and choosing a specific minimum role for each endpoint is forty-two guesses about someone else's business rules, whereas "a viewer does not write" needs no guessing. `belowWriteFloor` in `proxy.ts` refuses any mutating method below `editor`, ahead of the rate limiter so a refused write does not also burn quota; handlers already demanding `manager`/`admin` are untouched. Exemptions are writes a viewer makes about THEMSELVES rather than the business: terminal layouts, intel pin/dismiss, telemetry. Unknown or missing roles rank 0 and are denied. 6 tests. **Still owed:** the floor answers "may this user write at all", not "should THIS endpoint need manager". Seeding templates and deleting integrations plausibly want a higher bar than editor, and that is a per-endpoint judgement for the owner.
- 🟡 **12.6 / A06** SQL injection — **raw-SQL surface swept 2026-08-02; the rest of A06 (command/template/formula/CSV) not started.** Every `$queryRawUnsafe` / `$executeRawUnsafe` in `src/` was read. Three are safe by construction and stay: `intel/scheduler.ts` binds `$1`, `prisma-app.ts` is a static string (and is a good control in itself — a boot-time assertion that shouts if `DATABASE_URL_APP` ever points at a BYPASSRLS role), and `chunked-create-many.ts` interpolates a SAVEPOINT name that a regex already constrains to `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`. One was changed: `with-org-scope.ts` built the tenant GUC by concatenation, and now binds it — `set_config('app.organization_id', $1, true)`, proven equivalent to `SET LOCAL` against production before the swap. **The first version of this note claimed it was an open injection hole; that was wrong and is corrected here.** A `^[a-z0-9]{20,32}$` guard has stood at the top of that function since Phase 5.2 and rejects anything that could break out of a string literal — the hostile-input test fails at the validator, not at the statement. The change is defence in depth on the one line that decides which tenant a caller IS, not a patched vulnerability. The call-site gate now also rejects a `set_config('app.…')` written without `is_local = true`, which leaks the tenant across pooled connections exactly as a non-LOCAL `SET` does.
- 🟡 **12.7 / A07** Callback authenticity — **swept 2026-08-02. There are no inbound webhooks**; the only session-less entry points are the two `/api/cron/*` routes, which the proxy admits via `publicPaths` because a scheduler carries no session and the jobs legitimately span every organization. Their Bearer secret is therefore the entire boundary in front of a market-feed refresh and a mailed trade digest. Both already fail CLOSED when `CRON_SECRET` is unset (503, refuse to run) — the right direction and the harder half — and the secret IS configured on production, verified. Fixed: the comparison was `!==`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte; now `crypto.timingSafeEqual` behind `bearerMatches`, with the length check kept because `timingSafeEqual` throws on a mismatch and a failed auth attempt must not become a 500. **Severity stated honestly: over HTTP, network jitter swamps the signal and no exploit of a JS string compare across a real network has been demonstrated. It is fixed because the fix is four lines, not because an attack is expected.** 5 tests. **Still open:** no replay protection — a captured cron request can be resent until the secret rotates. Bounded by the jobs being idempotent-ish (advisory-locked feed refresh, a digest email) rather than by any control, so it needs a nonce or timestamp window if these ever gain side effects.
- 🟡 **12.8 / A08** Supply chain — **inventoried 2026-08-02, and one control turns out to be already live and worth knowing about.** npm is blocking install scripts for 9 packages under its `allowScripts` policy — `@parcel/watcher`, `@prisma/client`, `@prisma/engines`, `@sentry/cli`, `msgpackr-extract`, `prisma`, `sharp`, `unrs-resolver`, `@swc/core` — which is the single highest-value supply-chain control there is, since a malicious postinstall is how this class of compromise usually lands. `ignore-scripts` is `false`, so this is npm's own allowlist rather than a repo setting, and it is therefore **not pinned by anything in this repo**: an npm downgrade or a CI image change silently restores arbitrary postinstall execution. Note also that Prisma's postinstall being blocked means `prisma generate` must run explicitly — CI does. **Not done:** no lockfile-integrity gate beyond `package-lock.json` being committed, no provenance/attestation checks, no dependency-review action on PRs, and no pinned CI runner digests. See A09 for the CVE inventory, which is the other half of this.
- 🟡 **12.9 / A09** Dependency CVEs — **inventoried and triaged 2026-08-02; upgrades deliberately NOT applied.** `npm audit --omit=dev`: **19 vulnerabilities in production dependencies — 2 critical, 9 high, 7 moderate, 1 low.** The three that matter for this product: **`@auth/core` ≤0.41.2 (critical, CVSS 7.5)** — `getToken()` throws an uncaught exception on a malformed Bearer header, i.e. a DoS on the authentication path, plus a homoglyph-normalisation issue in the email normaliser; fix available, non-breaking. **`next` (high, CVSS 7.5 ×2)** — DoS with Server Components; fix available. **`expr-eval` (high, CVSS 7.3) — NO FIXED VERSION EXISTS**, prototype pollution plus "does not restrict functions passed to evaluate", and it is the engine every indicator formula runs through. Investigated rather than accepted: unreachable here for two reasons, and both are the kind that quietly stop being true. The parser is built with `assignment: false`, and expr-eval's prototype pollution is written as an assignment expression; and formulas are not user input — **there is no API anywhere in `src/app` that creates or updates an `IndicatorDefinition`**, verified by search, so a formula reaches the engine only from a seed script run by someone who already has database access. `formula-engine.hardening.test.ts` pins the first (someone tidying that options object would re-open a CVSS 7.3 without touching anything named "security"); the second is guarded by the absence of a route, which no test can assert — if an indicator-editing API is ever added, that file is the reason to revisit the dependency. **Upgrades left for the owner on purpose:** a lockfile change lands mid-demo while imports are being run against production, and `npm audit fix` on `@auth/core` touches the login path. Recommended order once there is a quiet window: `@auth/core` (critical, auth), `next`, `fast-uri`, `brace-expansion` — all non-breaking — then re-run the audit. `@anthropic-ai/sdk` needs a MAJOR (0.115.0) and should be scheduled separately.
- 🟡 **12.10 / A10** Session, CSRF, headers, TLS — **measured against production 2026-08-02; headers fixed, TLS remains the owner's.** **CSRF is covered and it was worth confirming rather than assuming**, because 117 mutating routes carry no CSRF token of their own: `curl -i http://46.225.60.142/api/auth/csrf` shows the session cookies set `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax`, and Lax is precisely what stops a cross-site POST/PUT/DELETE from carrying the session. Sessions are JWT with a 1h `maxAge` and a per-refresh DB re-read of role and organization, so a revoked role stops working within the hour rather than at token expiry. **`Secure` is absent** — there is no TLS to require — so the session cookie crosses the network in cleartext; that is the same owner-gated gap as the commented-out TLS block in `deploy/nginx/budgetpro.conf`, and it is the single largest remaining exposure in this phase. **Three response headers were missing entirely** (verified by curl; nginx sets none either) and are now set in `proxy.ts`: `X-Frame-Options: DENY` — this is a financial terminal with one-click plan purge and data reset, and framing it under an overlay turns a destructive action into a misplaced click; `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` — the app serves back bytes it was given (XLSX exports, `/api/help-videos/[file]`); `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` — terminal URLs carry company codes. Applied at **every** one of the proxy's seven exits, not just the last: `/login` leaves through the first, and wrapping only the terminal return would have left the page that most needs framing protection without it while looking done. A test asserts no bare `return NextResponse` survives in the file. **Deliberately not added:** HSTS (browsers ignore it over HTTP — it belongs with the certificate, and a test pins its absence so it is a decision rather than an oversight) and a real CSP (needs a nonce threaded through the Next render path; a wrong one breaks the app silently). **XSS sinks:** one `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, in `PlansTab.tsx`, fed by `t.raw()` from the repo's own message catalogue — not user input, but it is the one place a translation string becomes markup.
- ✅ **12.11 / A11** SSRF — **swept 2026-08-02, no finding.** Recorded so the next audit does not redo it. Every outbound host the server contacts is a hard-coded literal: `api.eia.gov`, `api.open-meteo.com`, `archive-api.open-meteo.com`, `api.worldbank.org`, `api.exchangerate.host`, `cbar.az`, `comtradeapi.un.org`, `query1.finance.yahoo.com`, `quickstats.nass.usda.gov`, `serpapi.com`, `api.scrapingdog.com`, `www.fao.org`, `www.stat.gov.az`. No endpoint is user-, DB- or env-supplied: `CommodityAdapterOptions` carries only `fetchImpl` (a test seam), and `google-trends-az`'s `proxyUrl` parameter is never passed anything but its hard-coded default outside tests — the `my-proxy.local` / `custom.proxy` hosts in the tree are fixtures. The web crawler, the obvious candidate, does not fetch at all: it validates model-returned URLs with `new URL()` and STORES them. **Re-open if** an adapter ever takes its base URL from `Organization.settings` or an admin form, which is the shape this would arrive in.
- 🟡 **12.12 / A12** Backups and restore — **measured on production 2026-08-02, and the backup was RESTORED rather than assumed.** What exists and works: `deploy/update-prod.sh` takes a verified `pg_dump` before every deploy — 149 archives, 117 MB, oldest 2026-06-25, five of them from today alone. **Restore rehearsal performed**, because a backup nobody has restored is a hypothesis: the newest pre-deploy dump was loaded into a scratch database on the same server, `psql` exit 0 with zero errors, and every count matched the live database exactly — `budget_lines` 44,173, `indicator_values` 6,460, `companies` 7, `budget_actuals` 0, **and all 92 RLS policies came back**, which matters because a restore that silently dropped them would come up with the tenant boundary gone. Scratch database dropped afterwards; only the four expected databases remain. **The real gaps, none of which I can close from here:** (1) **every backup sits on the same host as the database it protects** — no offsite copy and no remote target configured, so ransomware, a disk failure or a compromised root takes the data and its backups together; (2) **nothing is immutable** — root can delete or rewrite any archive, which is precisely what A12 names; (3) **backups are pre-deploy only** — there is no scheduled dump, so on a week without deploys there is no point-in-time protection at all (today's five deploys make coverage look denser than the policy actually is); (4) **retention is unbounded** — 149 files and growing with no pruning, on a disk at **85% (61G of 75G used)**, which will eventually fail a deploy at the exact moment the backup is needed. (1)–(3) need a destination and credentials the owner has to choose; (4) is a pruning policy, deliberately not implemented unilaterally because deleting backups is destructive.
- 🟡 **12.13 / A13** Residual risk — **first consolidated pass 2026-08-02.** Written below rather than as a separate document, so it cannot drift from the findings it summarises.

### Residual risk after the 2026-08-02 pass

Two defects were found and closed, both fail-open guards rather than missing ones — which is the pattern worth naming: **every gap this audit found was a control that existed and did not cover what it appeared to cover.** The call-site RLS gate checked call sites and not tables. The proxy's path rules were rate limits that read as RBAC. The job endpoint checked a tenant only when one was present. A checklist that asks "is there a control?" would have passed all three.

**Ranked by what would actually hurt, today:**

| # | Risk | Why it ranks here | Owner action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **No TLS.** Prod is plain-IP HTTP; the session cookie has no `Secure` flag and crosses the network in cleartext. | Anyone on-path takes an admin session. Every other control in this list assumes the session is not stolen. | Certificate + uncomment the nginx TLS block + add HSTS in the same change. |
| 2 | **Backups share a host with the database**, none immutable, none offsite. | Restore is proven to work (rehearsed, 92 RLS policies and every row count matched) — but one compromised root deletes the data and the proof together. | Choose an offsite target; then a scheduled dump, not just pre-deploy. |
| 3 | **`@auth/core` critical CVE** on the authentication path, plus 8 more highs. | Fix exists and is non-breaking; only left undone to avoid a lockfile change mid-demo. | `npm audit fix --omit=dev` in a quiet window. |
| 4 | **Disk at 85%** with 149 unpruned backups. | Fails a deploy at the moment the backup matters. | Retention policy — not applied unilaterally, deleting backups is destructive. |
| 5 | **Per-endpoint role review** still owed; the write floor answers "may this user write", not "should this need manager". | Bounded: no viewer can write anything now. | Owner decides which endpoints deserve a higher bar. |
| 6 | **No replay protection on `/api/cron/*`**, no CSP, no lockfile-integrity gate, `Organization.settings.apiKeys` would store a key in plaintext. | Each bounded today by circumstance rather than control. | Schedule; none is urgent. |

**30/60/90:** *30* — TLS (1) and the dependency fix (3); together they close the only two items an outside attacker could use today. *60* — offsite immutable backups (2) and backup retention (4). *90* — per-endpoint roles (5), CSP with a render-path nonce, cron replay protection, and encryption for the API-key setting before that screen is ever used.

**What this pass did NOT cover, so the phase stays 🟡:** 12.1 brute-force protection is paused by the owner and was not resumed; no dynamic testing was done at all — everything here is static reading plus direct production measurement, so an authenticated-session exploit chain would not have been found; and no dependency-review or provenance controls were added.

**Current gate:** A01 is `NOT_TESTED` and awaits explicit owner permission for
read-only code/config inspection plus safe local/staging tests. All later
controls remain blocked by the serial-audit rule.

## Phase 13: Import assistant — a tool, not a notification (NEW 2026-08-01, owner-requested)

**Owner question that triggered this:** «тут пишет, что три листа не смог прочесть — как теперь финансисту решить, или отдельно добавить, или понять почему не смогло прочесть? тут нужна не просто ассистентность, а реальный рабочий инструмент, который будет работать, исправлять, просить добавлять вручную либо говорить, что и как дальше сделать, чтобы получить всю инфу».

**The moment it was asked.** A live preview reported *"3 sheets could not be read — check them"* and listed `Tech`, `Satış İcmalı`, `Müştəri İcmalı` in one amber block. Two of the three cost nothing: `Tech` is a `Product | Yes/No` reference list with no financial data, and `Satış İcmalı` is a summary of what two other sheets already import in detail. The third cost four indicators — 371 customer rows reaching nothing — and had been failing on **every run since at least 2026-07-31**, where the identical warning sits verbatim in `warning-groups.test.ts`. Nothing on screen distinguished them.

**The governing principle, and it is not negotiable: the model proposes a READING, deterministic code produces the NUMBERS, and the file's own subtotals are the referee.** The model emits a shape descriptor — header row, name column, value columns, dimension columns, orientation — which is data: showable, confirmable, storable in a template, diffable between runs. It never emits an amount.

This is not caution for its own sake. Every defect closed on 2026-08-01 was found by comparing against a total the client had already computed: `PLF.03`, `PLF.08`, `PLF.10` and `Ümumi satış`. Each tied to the cent, and each disagreement was a real defect — 25,674,666 AZN of subsidies sitting in revenue, 1,677,015 of adjustments dropped, 132,770,310 about to land under the wrong account names. Net profit was correct throughout all of it.

**Build order is 13.1 first, deliberately.** Cross-footing protects what already works *and* everything the model adds later. Shipping 13.2 before it would be a new way to be wrong.

| # | Task | Evidence | Est. | Status |
|---|------|----------|------|--------|
| 13.1 | **The referee: cross-foot every sheet against the file's own totals, and say so when it agrees.** Generalise what was done by hand today. For each parsed sheet look for a subtotal the workbook computes itself and never imports (`PLF.03/08/10`, the `Ümumi satış` row, a balance-sheet total), compare it to the bottom-up sum, and report the comparison as a first-class result. Agreement must be *stated*, not implied by silence: "the sheet's own PLF.10 matched" is the sentence a finance director is looking for. Turns a green verdict from "I wrote what I parsed" into "I read what you have" — the gap 11.71 documents and the reason a parse-level loss can pass `db-readback`. **Storage and survival.** `BudgetLine.origin` / `correctionReason` / `correctionBy` / `correctionAt` / `correctionReviewAt`, all nullable with no backfill — NULL means "came from a workbook", which is all 44,173 live rows — plus two partial indexes. Corrections are excluded from the clean-slate archive, from the `purgeArchivedFirst` hard-delete AND from the collateral-guard count, so all three agree. The mock was taught the filter BEFORE the survival test was written, so that test is capable of failing rather than passing against an unimplemented predicate.

**And it found a second problem the design had not anticipated.** The post-write reconciliation reads the database back and compares it to what was parsed; a surviving correction on an imported account — the common case — became an `extra`, and any `extra` is an unconditional red that aborts the group. The first correction anyone made would have turned every later import of that file red, and the feature would have been abandoned inside a week. The readback now excludes corrections for the same reason the archive does: its claim is "the rows I WROTE match what I parsed".

**Write API.** `POST/GET /api/budgeting/corrections`. POST validates through the same pure `rejectCorrection` a UI will use, so the two cannot drift; answers each refusal with a sentence rather than a code; resolves account and plan through RLS so a foreign id is a 404 rather than a foreign-key error confirming it exists elsewhere; writes the `origin` stamp plus a self-describing `sourceDocument`; and logs `budget_correction_create` — the row records the CLAIM, the audit log records the MUTATION, and only the log survives the row being archived. **Subject to the period lock, deliberately not exempt:** "the period is closed" and "the number is wrong" are both true at once, and the resolution is a conversation with whoever locked it, not a side door. **Does not recompute inline** — that is the pipeline's job and it is async above 50 pairs; firing it here would let the caller believe the derived figures had moved when for a large company they have not. GET is the review queue, flagged rows first.

**The review flag is written.** After every import, corrections surviving in the touched companies × year are stamped `correctionReviewAt` and a `CORRECTIONS TO REVIEW:` warning names the count. Non-fatal: an unflagged correction is the status quo, an aborted import is a regression. Flag, never resolve — the platform cannot tell whether the new rows supersede the correction or merely coincide with it, so auto-clearing silently reverts a decision and auto-keeping silently doubles it.
