### 13.6 — how manual correction has to work, and why it is not an edit box

Written out here because the obvious implementation is the wrong one, and it is
obvious enough that a future session will reach for it.

**The tempting shape: let someone type over the number.** Either the indicator
value on the terminal, or the budget row in the P&L. Rejected, for four reasons
that are each individually sufficient.

1. *An edited indicator produces two truths.* The indicator is derived. Typing
   `58,880,102` over a wrong `72,333,200` leaves the P&L tab, the drill-down,
   every export and the board deck still showing the old number, because they
   read the rows, not the indicator. The screen would agree with the client and
   the reports would not.
2. *It makes the statement check circular.* 11.91 compares a derived figure
   against the workbook's own subtotal. If a person can type the derived figure,
   the natural thing to type is the subtotal — and then it reconciles, by
   construction, having verified nothing. A check whose input can be hand-set to
   its own expected value is not a check.
3. *Recompute owns that column.* An override would have to be either erased on
   the next recompute (useless) or permanently exempt the cell from its formula
   (a spreadsheet with extra steps, and one nobody would remember agreeing to).
4. *Mutating an imported row destroys the only faithful copy.* The imported rows
   are what the workbook said. That is what makes re-import safe, what makes the
   cross-foot meaningful, and what lets anyone answer "did we read it wrong, or
   was it wrong?". Editing in place burns the evidence to fix the symptom.

**The shape to build: a correction is a new row, attributed and reversible.**

- **An adjustment, not an edit.** A `BudgetLine` (or `OperationalFact`) written
  by a person, against a named account and period, with an amount, a reason, an
  actor and a timestamp. The imported rows stay exactly as parsed. Derived
  figures move because the underlying sum moved, which means the terminal, the
  P&L, the exports and the deck all move together — the thing an override
  cannot do.
- **Marked everywhere, forever.** Same rule as 11.66's provenance dots and
  11.91's ≠ ring: a total containing hand-entered money must never be
  indistinguishable from one that does not. A corrected figure carries its own
  marker and its own tooltip naming who corrected it and why.
- **It must survive a re-import, and that is the hard part.** The import
  clean-slates `planId × footprintCompanyIds × year`
  (`import-batch.ts:217-260`), so a naive adjustment row sitting in that scope
  is archived by the next run of the same file — the correction silently
  un-applies, which is worse than never having offered one. Corrections must be
  **excluded from the archive scope by provenance** (they name no workbook), and
  then **flagged for review after any re-import that touched their account and
  period**: the new file may already contain the fix, and applying both is a
  double correction. Flag, do not auto-resolve — the platform cannot know
  whether the new rows supersede the correction or coincide with it.
- **A correction is not a reconciliation.** After correcting, the 11.91 pass
  re-runs and the value either now agrees with the statement or does not.
  `lastReconciledAt` is written by the check, never by the act of correcting.
  This is the whole reason the pass is a separate re-runnable step over stored
  values rather than a side effect of the import.

**13.7 — the other half.** Sometimes the platform is right and the workbook is
wrong. AZSF 2025 is the live case: the block does not cross-foot in either
direction, so its ≠ can never be cleared by fixing our data. Without a way to
accept a difference — named person, stated reason, recorded — the only way to
silence the marker is to falsify a row, and the feature would have created the
exact behaviour it exists to prevent. An accepted difference stays visible as
*accepted*, never as *matched*.

### What the assistant must never do

Stated as prohibitions because each one has a dated cost in this repo.

- **Never adjust a number.** The display-layer compensator in `coa-role.ts` that "fixed" a sign stood from 2026-07-15 and put 25,674,666 AZN in the wrong line while every total stayed correct.
- **Never resolve an ambiguity silently.** The 2025 sheet files three different subsidy types under the single code `PLF.07.02.04`; a map keyed on the code alone had to get it wrong, and picking one would have been invisible.
- **Never treat "the total agrees" as proof.** Net profit tied throughout every defect above. Composition is what breaks.
- **Never let a classification be non-deterministic in a demo.** `Satış İcmalı` classified as `OPS_FACTS` in July and `INFO_SUMMARY` on 2026-08-01 — same sheet, same file, different runs. This is the argument for the model *proposing* and the template *deciding*.

### Prerequisite already met

11.84 shipped the briefing contract these stages fill in: **what is in it / what you lose / what to do**, with deliberately-skipped sheets demoted out of the amber block entirely. 13.2–13.5 exist to make the third part an action rather than advice.

## Changelog

- **2026-08-02 (Phase 11.92 — a twelve-month budget minus a five-month actual, printed as a −13.9M variance)** — The P&L page showed `BÜDCƏ 14.2M · FAKT 271k · KƏNARLAŞMA −13.9M · 2%` with nothing saying the two sides cover different amounts of time. Both figures are exactly right and tie to the client's own workbook: 14,213,417 is `PLF Budget 2026`'s own `PLF.08` across twelve months, 271,160 is `PLF Actual 2026`'s across **five** (January–May, measured on the file). Most of that "variance" is simply the seven months that have not happened, and the `2%` beside it is an execution ratio in early August, not a verdict. The KPI card above was worse: it captioned that five-month actual total **"Annual budget"** — wrong basis and wrong span in two words, on the one number a reader anchors to. Same failure as the 72.3M revenue and the 373M balance sheet — the number is correct and the sentence around it is not, which is the only kind of error that survives every arithmetic check. Fixed by deriving coverage from the same series the chart draws (so caption and bars cannot disagree), captioning the card with what is actually in it rather than what someone assumed would be, and putting an amber line under the variance tiles whenever the two spans differ. The dead `pnlKpiAnnualBudget` key is deleted from all three catalogues rather than left to be reused. **Deliberate limits:** the caveat appears only when the spans actually differ and never on a full year or an empty one — a warning that never retires is furniture; a non-contiguous year is listed month by month instead of being smoothed into a range, because a hole mid-year is a finding; and zero is read as "no data" since these monthly maps are dense and zero-filled, which can only add a caveat, never suppress one.

- **2026-08-02 (Phase 11.91 — the product could say where a number came from and never whether it was right)** — `IndicatorValue.lastReconciledAt` is one of two fields the decision-grade gate requires and had no writer anywhere in the product; only `audit-company.cjs` wrote it, a manual CLI that has never run on this data. So every coloured cell was permanently uncertified with no reachable state in which it cleared. The check that was missing is the one a human did by hand on 2026-08-01, four times, finding a real defect each time: these sheets compute their own `PLF.01/03/08/10`, the importer never reads them (it sums the leaves), and that makes them an oracle the client has already agreed with. 72.3M of revenue was a plausible figure for this holding for a year; against the client's own `PLF.01` it falls in one comparison. Now: a pure comparator over six P&L-answerable codes, a **separate re-runnable pass over stored values** (not folded into recompute — "check this again" must not mean "recompute everything", and reading the stored row is the one place a write bug can surface), three new columns, and a rule that keeps the gate honest — `lastReconciledAt` still means "last time it PASSED", a mismatch gets its own status/expected/checked-at, and a failure **clears** any older pass-stamp so the gate cannot read green while the screen says the number is wrong. On screen a mismatch is a fuchsia ring plus `≠` on the tile, a count in the heat-map header, and both figures with the gap in Panel 3 — deliberately outside the status palette, because a red cell that is also wrong is the worse case and must be distinguishable from a red cell that is right. The panel does not name which number is wrong; in this dataset both have been. **Known limits:** only the year period is reconcilable (these are FY totals — checking an April margin against one would manufacture a mismatch on every month of every company); six indicators, all P&L, with balance-sheet totals unwired; every existing row reads NULL and keeps saying "not checked" until a re-import runs the pass, with **no backfill**, because inventing "matched" for values nobody compared to anything is the lie this exists to expose; and seeing a discrepancy is not yet being able to fix one — the correction design is 13.6/13.7, including why an edit box over the number is the wrong shape (it makes this check circular, produces two truths, and burns the only faithful copy of what the workbook said). The visual gate could not run in the authoring environment (no `E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, no local DB) — both markers render only on `reconStatus === 'mismatched'` and no row carries that yet, so the baseline is *expected* unmoved, not verified.

- **2026-08-01 (Phase 11.85 — two charts of accounts, one unique index: 48,735,978 ₼ about to be filed under the wrong names)** — `PLF Actual 2025` and the 2026 sheets renumbered 155 codes against each other, and `chart_of_accounts` has one name per code with no year. Since `resolveOrCreateAccountId` never renames an existing row, the pending 2025 re-import would have posted 16,428,573 ₼ of processed-corn revenue under "Revenue from Sale of Almond" and 37 accounts' worth of the same, with every total still correct and every check still green. The mapping is now the client's own wording — match the normalised label among leaf codes, keep the 2025 code's section when two match — expressed as a derivation function whose output is the checked-in table, with a test that re-derives it from the workbook and demands the file byte for byte. Keying on (code, LABEL) rather than code is what makes it correct: `PLF.07.02.04` carries three different subsidies on the 2025 sheet, and a code-keyed pass mislabels 4,977,039 ₼ of them. A 2025 account whose code 2026 took over is minted as `<code>.FY2025` with its own name; an account that would duplicate an existing one under another code is named in a warning rather than created in silence. The number was arithmetically correct and epistemically empty, and it was not confined to the deck: it fires `RULE_COMPANY_CRITICAL_COMPOSITE` (`scoreMax` 40), which writes an `AlertEvent` row. The census found the mirror-image case is **more common**: 27 pairs of `100 green` computed from two commodity cells on AZSF / CPC / PROMALT across May–Nov 2025. A clean bill of health from a wheat price.

**Decision: withhold, do not qualify.** The rejected alternative was to keep publishing the number greyed out with a low-confidence caption. It loses on the one criterion the task exists to satisfy — the hero renders 96px of number against 14px of caption, and in a screenshot, a photocopy or a PDF pasted into email the number survives the journey and the caveat does not. `0` is the most verdict-shaped glyph in the product; rendering it grey keeps the costume and removes the badge. The decisive asymmetry: **withholding fails on a reader who wants a number and does not get one; qualifying fails on a reader who gets a number that is not one.** The first is recoverable in the room; the second is not, because nobody asks. Also rejected: **splitting by surface** (withhold on the deck, qualify in the terminal) — `build-snapshot` reads the same cells as the matrix route and the census confirms the two cell sets are identical on this data (0 of 204 pairs differ), so two policies means a board member reading `43` on slide 3 and `R— 2/28` on the screen behind it. What DOES split by surface is rendering: a 9px chip gets `R— 2/28`, the deck hero gets a full sentence, the XLSX gets a text token. Same rule, three registers.

**The rule lives at the chokepoint, for the reason 11.71 established.** `computeCompositeScore` is the only function in the repo that turns cells into a number, and the other eleven call sites either call it or re-aggregate its output. `MIN_SCORING_CELLS = 4`; below it the function returns `score: null`, `band: 'unknown'` — the state `CompositeScore` already modelled and every display site already handled, so nothing regresses silently, and the three sites that re-derive a band from the number are all null-safe and cannot mis-colour a withheld company. Added alongside: a **required** `coverage: 'none' | 'insufficient' | 'full'`. Required, not optional, and this is the one place the churn was worth paying: the two withheld states are already distinguishable by arithmetic, but *five surfaces must print different sentences for them* («none of the 28 applicable indicators has figures» vs «2 of 28 — at least 4 needed»), and re-deriving that predicate at five sites is 11.66's failure mode transcribed into copy. `tsc --noEmit` became the checklist. Invariant every consumer may rely on: **`score === null` ⟺ `coverage !== 'full'`**. Shipped as a module constant, deliberately NOT org config — `criticalComposite.scoreMax` is per-org; a configurable coverage floor is a knob an org can use to configure its way back into one-cell scores.

**Three independent arguments land on 4, and the window is exactly one wide.** *(a) Provenance.* Cross-tabbing the 143 scored (company, period) pairs on production against the repo's own `indicatorProvenance()`: of the pairs with 1, 2 or 3 contributing cells (22 + 44 + 18), **not one** contains a client-supplied figure — every one is commodity feeds and a rainfall forecast, computed whether or not the client ever uploaded anything. At 4, nine of eighteen do. So N≥4 withholds every purely-external low-coverage score and destroys **zero** scores containing a client figure. *(b) One cell must not decide the band.* At n=3, `[red, green, green]` averages 66.67 → rounds to **67 green**, and flipping one green to red gives 33.33 → **33 red**; rounding does it, the arithmetic alone hides it. At n=4 no assignment permits a single-flip green→red, and with production's real weights (0.7–1.5) maximum single-cell influence falls to 25.0–30.2%, the first value below the 33-point amber band. *(c) External-feed floor.* Every company in this org receives 1–4 cells free from org-wide feeds (rainfall, commodity vol, sugar/wheat price, FAO index), so a guard at 2 or 3 sits *inside* that floor and guards nothing — a company with an entirely empty ledger would still publish a number. **Against 5:** it is the only count reaching zero degenerate scores and it reaches it by suppressing the corpus's one true signal (EDEN's nine `0/100 (4/28)`, three of whose four cells are customer-concentration reds, 94% of revenue in three customers) and by blanking the entire 2025 annual row — the terminal's default landing screen would show no score for anybody. **Against relative** (e.g. 20% of `totalCount`): the precision of a mean depends on the number of samples, not the size of the frame; `totalCount` already moves whenever a definition or an applicability rule lands, and a band flipping because someone edited the catalogue is not a risk signal; «fewer than 4 indicators» verifies against `2/28` at a glance, «below 20% coverage» does not; and it would hold the agro companies to a stricter standard purely because the agro template defines five more indicators. **Rejected as the gate: provenance itself** — it produces the cleanest blanks in the option set (50 surviving pairs, every one touching a client figure) but it bounds nothing: one client-supplied red gross margin passes it and still yields 0/100 from one cell, which is the reported bug in a new costume. It stacks cleanly on top if the owner later wants strict over consistent; not shipped because it blanks the whole 2025 landing screen.

**Parent roll-ups: drop the withheld child from the mean, keep it in the denominator, print the revenue share.** `deriveParentComposites` already filtered on `score !== null`; the predicate is now the explicit `coverage === 'full'` (same set, and it cannot drift if the null invariant is ever relaxed). The real change is the denominator: `totalCount` sums over **all** children and `contributingCount` only over included ones — before this both summed over included children, so a subsidiary dropped for thin coverage vanished from the frame too, i.e. the code picked *drop, and conceal the drop*. AZSEKER 2026 is now 41/153, not 41/97; 153 is the truth, that most of the holding's indicator surface is empty. This is consistent with 11.71 rather than against it: 11.71 shrank the denominator for cells that could NEVER score, and an under-covered child COULD. New `children: {scored, total, revenueCoveredPct}`, set only here, because a board reads «4 of 6 subsidiaries scored · 88% of holding revenue». **Why dropping and not averaging:** averaging the withheld child in at its own low-coverage score is the reported bug at holding scale — the deck hero read **49** for 2026 annual precisely because DASTAN's and SAF's rainfall forecasts entered as two whole zeros; excluding them gives **74**, a 25-point error on the largest glyph in the deck caused by two cells. Imputing (parent mean, sector median) means inventing a number for a company we are simultaneously refusing to score. `MIN_SCORING_CELLS` deliberately does NOT apply at parent level — the parent's unit is children, not cells, and that branch builds an object literal rather than calling the leaf scorer, so the gate reaches every leaf and no parent by construction. Rejected: a low-confidence fallback that averages insufficient children when none qualifies («100, low confidence, over six children none of which is trustworthy» reintroduces at holding level exactly what the leaf gate removes); a **revenue-materiality gate** (principled, and unverifiable from the data on hand — shipping a second threshold that may or may not blank the holding in nine production periods is a coin flip, so the materiality *disclosure* ships and the *gate* does not); and pooling children's cells into one large set (discards revenue weighting and double-counts correlated inputs — three companies × the same two wheat-price indicators is two observations, not six).

**Alerts.** `company-critical-composite` now requires `coverage === 'full'` — a clause redundant against the null invariant and written anyway, because this is the rule the bug report is about and it should state its own precondition. No new threshold entry: the gate rides on the object the rule already computes, so the badge and the alert can never disagree about who is scorable. Counterfactual across all 34 periods **with DASTAN and SAF activated** (which is what onboarding does): **31 → 9** matches, and all nine are EDEN's genuine concentration reading; without this change, the moment those two go active, 22 `AlertEvent` rows saying «composite score 0/100 (1/28 indicators)» get written. New **`company-low-coverage`** at `severity: 'warning'` — removing an alert and shipping silence is not an improvement, and the brief's own constraint is that «not enough data» must read as a measurable fact; it fires on both `none` and `insufficient` (a company with zero indicator data is the stronger version of the same fact and generates no signal at all today), reads `MIN_SCORING_CELLS` directly so the two rules cannot drift, and is bounded by the persister's existing `status != pending` filter and annual-only invocation. **`company-mostly-red` is untouched**: it counts observed red cells, and an observation is not an inference — coverage gates inference. The two are permitted to coexist on one company; «we cannot grade you, and everything we can see is red» is more informative than either alone. It is unreachable on today's data, so no copy exists for it yet — flagged, not solved.

**Surfaces — wherever the score would have rendered, the coverage fraction renders.** Never a bare dash, never a blank cell, never a hidden row. Heat-map badge: the coverage block moved **above** the early return (it rendered only in the scored branch, so the one number that explains the dash was dropped exactly when it mattered) and now reads `◇R— 2/28` in grey with a title that names the state. CompanyTree chip: the `return null` is **deleted** — that was the one site in the product that violated «do not hide a company» outright, rendering code, trust badge and freshness with no risk marker at all. Snapshot badge takes the whole `CompositeScore` instead of an unwrapped `score`, which is why it had no coverage in either branch. Deck hero drops its `score !== null` guard — a bare «—» as the largest glyph with nothing under it is the worst blank in the product. `redSubCoCount` card: a withheld company's band is `'unknown'` so it silently left the `band === 'red'` filter while the context string kept saying «of 6 operational»; the card now names the excluded ones. XLSX: `s?.score ?? ""` wrote an **empty cell**, indistinguishable from «not computed», which breaks the client's own `AVERAGE`/`MIN` invisibly and sorts to whichever end Excel picks — and this is the one export a client re-sorts themselves; it writes a text token now, and the coverage column is always populated. Trend chart: `TrendPoint` gains `contributingCompanies`/`totalCompanies`, because this is the ONE site where the floor can *manufacture* a false trend rather than merely blank one — the cohort silently shrinks 4 → 2 between 2026-05 and 2026-06 and the line still plots a solid, connected, confident point. Narration: the comparator puts full-coverage companies first, each row carries `NOT_SCORED` with its fraction, and `SYSTEM_PROMPT` gains a hard constraint forbidding the model to call them healthy, at risk, best or worst — `boardDeck.evidence.scoreMethod` has always told the human reader; nothing had ever told the model. The batch fact-checker learns `4` as a scale constant, or it would flag the threshold the model was told as a fabricated figure. `heatMap.noScoreableIndicators` is deliberately NOT reused for the new states — «No scoreable indicators» is factually false for a company with 2 of 28, and the string stays scoped to `totalCount === 0`.

**Migration reality.** Terminal default landing (2025 annual): AZSF / CPC / PROMALT stay **70 green, unchanged**; EDEN goes to `R— 2/28`; and the AZSEKER root **gains a number it never had** — `CompanyTree` built `compositeByCode` only from `matrix.companies`, which is level-2 operational rows plus level-1 rows with `role='operational'`, and AZSEKER is `role='holding'`, so the root chip has received `null` for as long as it has existed. The score was always computed (`deriveParentComposites` keys off the children's `parentCompanyId`); it had no code to be found under. Closed by walking the company-tree prop here rather than by widening the matrix endpoint's entity universe — adding the holding to `matrixEntities` would also give it applicability rows, synthetic rollup cells and a HeatMap row, none of which this needs. **2026 annual — the planning year, where the client's data is:** all four visible companies keep their score unchanged (AZSF 73, CPC 89, EDEN 39, PROMALT 94); DASTAN and SAF go from `0/100 critical` to «not enough data — 1 of 28». The reported bug, gone, with zero collateral on 2026. Across all 34 periods, 84 of 143 scored pairs lose their number and the 61 pairs already showing a bare «—» gain a fraction; deck hero 2026 annual **49 → 74**, 2025 annual **57 → 70**. EDEN's nine genuine all-red readings survive, still scored, still alerting.

**What this ships knowingly broken, in the order it will bite.** (1) The gate cannot tell EDEN's four real cells from AZSF's four commodity cells: nine pairs survive at 4/23 with zero client data, publishing `70 green` on a wheat price — the same species of claim EDEN's 2/28 is withheld for. 4 is where the external-feed ceiling and the first real signal happen to collide **on this org**. (2) Removing data makes the holding look better — 2025 annual rises 57 → 70 because three amber children drop out, and a reader who does not read «3 of 6 subsidiaries scored» sees an improvement; disclosures get cropped, screenshotted and pasted into email. (3) Nine consecutive periods (2025-05…11, Q2, Q3) lose the holding number entirely; they read 100 today, and the honest explanation — that the 100 was two wheat-price cells — is not visible at a glance. (4) The threshold is a cliff and the cliff is where the data is: 18 pairs sit at exactly 3 and 18 at exactly 4, so 25% of all scored pairs are within one cell of the boundary and monthly periods will oscillate between «89 green» and «not enough data». Nothing here damps that. (5) `MIN_SCORING_CELLS` is calibrated on one org, two industries, 34 periods; «nothing below 4 has client data» is a property of this dataset, not a law, and needs a review gate at customer two. (6) The alert gate goes quiet on the way down — a subsidiary whose coverage falls from 12 to 3 stops firing `company-critical-composite` as it deteriorates; `company-low-coverage` fires instead, at `warning`, saying nothing about direction. A coverage-collapse detector belongs with the drift watchdog and is not built here. (7) The census is a replay: it imports the real helpers and reproduces production's `alert_events` 1:1, but only for annual periods, and most of the 84 withheld pairs are monthly and quarterly.

Gates: `npx tsc --noEmit` **0 errors** · `npx vitest run` **8047 passed / 121 skipped / 0 failed** (8021 | 121 before) · `npx next build` **exit 0**. New copy in `messages/{en,az,ru}.json` — 16 keys added, `boardDeck.evidence.scoreMethod` and both `trendBoundary` variants amended; key-identical across locales, distinct prose per locale, placeholder-parity green. **Not run: the visual-baseline E2E gate**, which `HeatMap.tsx` / `subcomponents.tsx` / `CompanyTree.tsx` require before commit — there is no dev server on port 3000 in this environment and `E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is unset, so all three specs fail at login rather than at a screenshot diff. It must be run on a machine that has both before this lands. No migration, no production write, no deploy; production was read SELECT-only.

- **2026-07-31 (Phase 11.79 — «bring it back» brought back every generation; and one caption that was wrong every time)** — **P0, verified on production data.** `restoreRows` un-archived by SCOPE alone (`delete where.deletedAt; where.deletedAt = { not: null }`). The scope for `BudgetLine` is org + companyId + `plan:{year}` — a bucket, not an operation — and the bucket holds every generation the re-imports left behind, because `runImportBatch` archives the version it replaces and deliberately does not purge it (`purgeArchivedFirst` off; "pileup is harmless to reads"). Measured live: 33,923 `budget_lines` of which only 2,979 live, 12+ distinct archive timestamps, and 2026 budget alone carrying three generations (2045 + 1234 + 811) for one company-year. Pressing Restore would have made all three live at once and multiplied every financial statement, indicator and board-deck figure derived from them. The one narrowing the signature offered, `matchDeletedBy`, was never passed by any caller — and the doc comment claimed it was. **The key is the exact `deletedAt`**: `archiveStamp()` is called ONCE per operation and reused for every `updateMany` in it, `DateTime` is `timestamp(3)` and `new Date()` is millisecond-precision, so the stamp round-trips through the audit metadata losslessly and needs no tolerance window (a window is how the second generation creeps back). `archiveRows` / `resetCompanyImportData` / `archiveOrgOrphanBudgetLines` now record `metadata.archivedAt`; `restoreRows` REQUIRES it and matches on equality; the route 400s (`MISSING_ARCHIVE_KEY`) without it. **Fail closed on legacy events** — rows archived before this commit carry a `deletedAt` that no audit row names, and there is no way to reconstruct the generation boundary, so those deletions are listed on the screen with an explanation and NO button rather than falling back to the sweep. `archiveRows` also records a `breakdown` now, so the Restore panel names the one table it took instead of guessing four kinds. Rationale in full at ARCHIVE_GENERATION_KEY in `src/lib/server/archive.ts`; reproduced by `archive-generations.test.ts`, which builds the measured three-generation pile-up in memory, restores the middle one, and asserts 1234 live / 811 + 2045 still archived — plus a live comparison showing the pre-fix filter returning 4090. **Same pass, the regression the previous one introduced:** `restorePlan` dropped each category's `fate`, so `RestoreTask` printed one blanket «those come back when you upload the file again» over the whole "will not bring back" list. `indicatorValue` is `ALWAYS_INCLUDED` and in every per-company breakdown, so **100 %** of restore panels made a file promise for rows no file returns; with manual actuals ticked the same caption sat over `budgetActualManual`, whose delete-side copy says four steps earlier that re-uploading will NOT bring it back. Each line now carries its own fate (`restore.fate.reimport|permanent|recomputed`), ordered worst-first. **Six further copy defects closed**, each pinned by a catalogue test: the retention window is printed again on both the blast radius and the restore list, DERIVED from `SOFT_DELETE_RETENTION_DAYS` so it cannot drift from the cron (silence read as "no expiry" while a nightly job removes the rows); `restore.doneNothing` no longer states the one cause its own filter makes impossible; `removeCompany.keptNote` admits that hand-entered operational facts survive every task on the page and keep feeding the indicators; `radius.truth` admits the recompute rebuilds the alert history org-wide (`persistAlertEvents` deletes by `{organizationId, period}`); the "recalculated automatically, need nothing from you" clause switches to an honest one when the delete also removes the source rows; `RunResult` stops folding records into the row count (preview said 1877 rows + 17 records, the result panel said 1894 rows) and prints units in its category list. Also: `radius.scope` / `scopeAllYears` are ICU plurals — en and ru rendered «Across 1 companies» / «По 1 компаниям» on the most common delete on the screen; `removeCompany.permanentNote` no longer claims the compliance RECORDS are file-irrecoverable (the AI import writes them; only the write-backs are); `deleteAll.keptNote` no longer says "only the figures go" on the task that sends `includeUnscoped: true`; and the last two "90-day retention" comments in the delete path are gone. Gates: `tsc --noEmit` 0 · `vitest run` 8021 passed | 121 skipped (was 7975 | 121) · `next build` exit 0.

- **2026-07-31 (Phase 11.78 — the screen promised more than it delivers: recoverability, records, and the «All years» note)** — Two reviewers re-read the finished Delete data screen and found the same species of defect three times: a sentence derived from a static property of a category rather than from what the code will do for THIS request. **(1) P0 — «can be brought back from this page» was false for most deletes and always false for Tasks B and D.** `archive.ts` writes the audit metadata as `year: years.length === 1 ? years[0] : undefined` (three sites, verified before branching on it), and `RestoreTask` lists only events whose `year` is set — so a multi-year or all-years delete produces **no restorable entry at all**, and Tasks B and D are all-years by construction. The rows are soft-archived and an engineer can recover them; the OPERATOR, on this page, cannot. The rule now lives once, in `delete-request.ts` (`auditYearFor` — which `archive.ts` writes through — and `producesRestorableEvent`, which the UI asks). `BlastRadius` takes the request's `years` array instead of a count, and when the delete leaves no restorable event the clause and the group heading change to «Sistemdən çıxarılır, bazada saxlanılır — bu səhifədən qaytarıla bilməz» plus a caveat naming technical support as the only way back. **(2) P0 — records were absent from the headline, and one real case rendered as a lie.** `ledger.items` appeared in no clause: a company holding only compliance records rendered «0 sətir silinəcək.» in the largest bold line on the screen, directly above 12 permanently destroyed write-backs, with the red button enabled. Records cannot join `{rows}` (different unit), so they get two clauses carrying their own unit and a lead of their own for the rows-are-zero case. **(3) P0 — `years.allChipNote` claimed a deletion Task A cannot perform** («öz ili olmayan qeydləri də silir»), contradicting `what.recordsNote` and `radius.recordsKept` on the same screen: `categoriesFor` never returns `records` for Task A and `includeUnscoped` is never sent. Rewritten to say what «All years» does add (the rows the chips do not break down by year — operational figures and the sales plan) and to point the records at the task that owns them. **P1s in the same pass:** every clause now carries its unit in all three languages (ru had dropped it in four, en in three); the lead is a headline with no terminal stop and the clauses are capitalised sentences, one per line, so the ~200-character bold middot run and the lowercase-after-a-full-stop in az/ru are both gone; the restore panel derives its «will bring back» list, its «will not» list and the calls it fires from the breakdown the deletion recorded (`restorePlan`) instead of promising four data types and firing four calls that returned 0 — an event that archived nothing is no longer offered at all, a zero restore reports `restore.doneNothing` in amber rather than «0 sətir geri qaytarıldı» in green, and two new sentences say that indicators are not rebuilt by a restore and that a restore reaches every archived row for that company and year. The `{rows}` vs `expectRows` justification in `BlastRadius.tsx` was **wrong** and is corrected rather than papered over: `preview.rowsAffected` sums every breakdown bucket, records included, so on Tasks B and D it exceeds `{rows}` by exactly `ledger.items` — both numbers are right for what they measure, `{rows}` still equals the submit button, and the difference is now named on screen (pinned by a test asserting `rows + items === Σ breakdown`). No gate weakened, no wire-protocol change, no second token authority. Pinned by 54 new tests, including mutation-verified renders through the **real** az/ru/en catalogues (the production case, and case C with zero rows and non-zero records) — a key-shaped translator mock cannot see a lowercase clause after a full stop. `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors; `npx vitest run` **7975 passed / 121 skipped / 0 failed** (7921 before); `npx next build` exit 0. Knowingly not fixed, and still open: «3 qeyd» is a count of settings KEYS presented as a record count; Task B's empty state uses the multi-select sentence; `result.done.recompute` prints «(0 dəyər)»; the 207 panel prints company codes rather than names and `orphanTailRemains` conflates the two org sweeps; `adminDataArchive.actionArchive` says «arxivləndi» and the audit table prints the `__ORG_*` sentinels raw; the `ALL` token is still an English word the operator cannot read (localising it needs a DISPLAY counterpart off the single wire authority — not a second accepted token); and the P2 register pass on ~15 az / 8 ru strings. No migration, no production write, no deploy.

Pinned by 17 tests that drive the **real POST handler** with the **real** `gateFor` + `buildCommitRequest` output, across all four tasks × single/multi company × named/all years, plus one that still 400s on the pre-11.77 client's answer. - **2026-07-31 (Phase 11.76 — "Delete data": one comprehensible screen, and the preview finally counts what the reset deletes)** — Owner, twice: «удаление тут сейчас непонятное — пусть чтоб было легко, интуитивно, интерактивно, юзер-френдли: удалить что именно и за какие года, или все года», «должно быть удаление упрощённое по годам, простым понятным языком, и кнопка удалить всё». Two rival surfaces are now one. `ImportDataResetPanel` (a company dropdown, a bare year box and FOUR rival buttons on the AI Import page) is reduced to a three-line note, because **its premise was false**: an import batch clean-slates exactly what it writes (`import-batch.ts:217-260`), so a reset was never a step before re-uploading — presenting one as routine housekeeping put the most destructive action in the product directly in the path of a routine one. `DataArchiveForm` (the second deletion surface, same endpoint, `"ALL"` gate, **no preview**) is deleted, as is `import-reset-scopes.ts`, whose holding/company scope duality made "whole holding" and "whole group" mean different sets on two screens that neither named. **`/budgeting/admin/data-archive` is now task-first**: "what do you want to do?" → clear a year · remove a company · bring data back · ——— *cannot be undone* ——— delete everything. Task A asks which companies, which years (chips carrying real row counts from a new `yearIndex`, plus a separate All-years chip — **there is no field left that can be blanked into a wider scope**, which is how `2026` used to become every year with one backspace), what exactly (three plain bundles, with the nine named categories behind a "Choose exactly" disclosure), then counts before it writes. Reconstructing the widest scope by hand — every company AND all years — is **refused** and points at Task D: the widest scope now has exactly one door. The blast radius groups by fate — *can be brought back from this page* / *gone for good* / *comes back when you upload the file again* / *deleted and recalculated* — renders by mapping over the keys the response returns through one label+fate table (never a hardcoded key array, the exact bug that hid `salesBudgetLine` for a phase), counts records in *items* and never folds them into the row headline, and **replaces** the permanent clause rather than printing "0 gone for good". The gate is never weaker than before — a typed token, a reason and a fresh preview at every tier — but the token now says something: at one company it is that **company's code**, not the "ALL" the hand had already learned. Submit is dead at zero rows (the old check was `rowsAffected >= 0`, true of every number a count can return). **Four backend defects fixed, each with a test that fails without it:** (1) the preview never counted `salesForecast` while the whole-holding commit path hard-deleted it — nine confident numbers, then the group's sales forecast gone unannounced; (2) the reset transaction ran eight statements, including a `ProductLine.code` relation subquery and two unindexed prefix scans, on Prisma's **5-second default** — now `{ maxWait: 15_000, timeout: 120_000 }`, matching every import path; (3) the settings tail deleted all 14 `IMPORT_SETTINGS_KEYS` **regardless of year**, so "clear 2026" destroyed every court case, audit finding, risk-register row and every Compliance Hub close/assign/deadline/comment for all time — those records carry no year, so a year-scoped delete no longer reaches them, in the preview and in the reset; (4) `resetOrgSalesForecast` failing was swallowed and reported as a clean 200 (and was **never actually exercised**: it was missing from the handler test's `vi.mock`, so every "whole-holding" test called `undefined(...)` and the TypeError was caught silently). Also: `BudgetActual` split by provenance — hand-entered rows (`source: null`, documented unrecoverable) now survive unless explicitly asked for; `years[]`, `include[]`, `includeUnscoped`, `includeManualActuals` and an `expectRows` **409 drift guard** on both endpoints, all defaulting to the old behaviour; the period-lock gate tests **every** year in a multi-year delete; company ceiling 200 → 1000 (past 200 a "delete everything" was silently truncated, which also flipped `isWholeHolding` false so the org sweeps never fired); the history table finally shows `data_reset` rows, which it had never queried. Dead `SOFT_DELETE_RETENTION_DAYS = 90` removed — the live purge is **30** days and the UI was quoting the dead constant at users ("Restore is available within 90 days"), so the new copy prints no day count at all. `adminAiImport.reset.*` (40 keys, ~16 untranslated English) deleted; `adminDataDelete.*` added in real Azerbaijani and Russian across all three catalogues. `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors; `npx vitest run` **7885 passed / 121 skipped / 0 failed** (was 7811 before this work, 7761 at the phase baseline). No migration, no production write, no deploy.

- **2026-06-16 (Safety net — import clean-slate collateral-deletion GUARD across all batch tables + KPI hard-delete scoped to its metrics)** — Follow-up to the cross-plan budget-wipe (below): the user flagged recurring import data-corruption as the project's #1 problem and asked for the systemic cause, not another point-fix. **Root cause:** every import "clean-slates" (delete matching rows → insert), but the DELETE scope is hand-written per batch and must EXACTLY match the INSERT identity; there was no shared abstraction deriving one from the other and no post-import invariant against collateral deletion — so each new identity dimension (companyId on BS rows, budget+actual plans per year, per-entity sourceId on CF) silently drifted the delete broader than the insert → sibling data loss (2026-06-11 BudgetLine cross-plan; 2026-05-31 BS/CF cross-entity) or double-count (2026-06-03 readers missing deletedAt). DB evidence of recurrence: 5913 archived BudgetLine + 959 BS + 1199 CF rows across 3 actors, 05-20…06-11. **Fix (user chose "safety net now"):** (1) NEW `src/lib/onboarding/collateral-guard.ts` — table-agnostic `assertNoCollateralDeletion` throws `CollateralDeletionError` (rolls back the write tx) when `archivedCount > footprintLiveCount`, where the footprint is counted INDEPENDENTLY from the INSERTED rows' own identity (companies/plans/entities/metrics), NOT from the archive WHERE (non-circular, so it actually fires on drift). Wired into all four batches: `import-batch.ts` (BudgetLine — catches caller companyIds/planIds broader than rows), `bs-import-batch.ts` (BalanceSheetLine — caller planIds broader than rows), `cf-import-batch.ts` (CashFlowEntry — dropped entity-prefix scope), `kpi-import-batch.ts` (OperationalFact — caller companyIds broader than rows). (2) **KPI hard-delete fix** (the one irreversible path — OperationalFact has no soft-delete): the reset now scopes `deleteMany` AND the reconciliation read to `metric ∈ rows' metrics`, so re-importing one KPI no longer wipes the company's sibling metrics, and a zero-row parse deletes nothing (`metric: { in: [] }`) instead of wiping the whole date window. Semantics note: a metric absent from the new file now lingers (file is authoritative only for the metrics it parses) — accepted vs irreversible loss; an explicit delete-intent manifest is the follow-up if full replacement is ever needed. (3) **Codex nit** — added `organizationId` to the per-year `pl_ebitda` deleteMany in `production-adapter-handlers-financial.ts` (defense-in-depth cross-org guard on a destructive delete). **Tests:** +5 guard unit + 1 BudgetLine guard-trip + 3 KPI (metric-scope survives sibling / zero-row no-op / guard-trip) regression cases; mocks gained `count` + honor planId/metric/year; verified guards FAIL without the fix. tsc 0; full `src/lib/onboarding/` suite **631 green** + ai-import **175 green**. Reviewed by Codex (SHIP-WITH-NITS). **Known residual (tracked, not blocking):** CF guard can't catch a bad/shared sourceTag or the no-entityCode legacy fallback (no row-level key to compare); `production-adapter-handlers-soft.ts` İcmal delete (planId+sourceDocument) is outside the batch guard. - **2026-06-03 (Fix — SSE live-update listener permanently poisoned by one first-connect failure; explains the live `/api/events/stream` 503)** — Terminal bug-audit re-run (`we2d7o4h2`) P1 #2. `src/lib/events/postgres-listener.ts` `getClient()` assigned the connect IIFE to the module `clientPromise` singleton **before** `await client.connect()` resolved. The only reset (`clientPromise = null`) lived inside the `client.on('error')` handler — which is registered *after* a successful connect and fires on a client *event*, never on a `connect()`/`LISTEN()` **promise** rejection. So a single DB cold-start/restart/blip at the moment of the first subscribe after a deploy cached a permanently-**rejected** promise; every later `subscribe()` re-threw, the SSE route emitted an `error` event and closed, and live updates stayed dead **process-wide until redeploy** (the feature silently degraded to REST polling — hence P1 not P0). Fix: wrapped connect + both LISTEN queries in a `try/catch` that nulls the singleton and tears down the half-open client on any failure, so the next `subscribe()` retries a fresh connection; this also heals the reconnect-connect path (a reconnect whose connect rejected previously re-poisoned the singleton the same way). The connected client is bound to a `const` so the long-lived handler closures keep a non-nullable reference. +2 regression tests (connect-rejection and LISTEN-query-rejection each reset the singleton + tear down the half-open client; 7 listener tests total). tsc 0.
- **2026-06-03 (Fix — scoped (non-admin) manager's audit trail silently truncated; compliance gap)** — Terminal bug-audit re-run (`we2d7o4h2`) P1 #3. `GET /api/audit/events` fetched `take=limit+1` rows then applied the Phase 7.F sub-group RBAC filter **in JS** (the `IndicatorValue→company` map can't live in the Prisma `where` — `entityId` is a free-text polymorphic column, not a relation FK), but computed `hasMore`/`nextCursor` from the **post-filter** array. So whenever the limit+1 window contained an out-of-scope `Company`/`IndicatorValue` event (imports, threshold overrides, recomputes — among the most common audit rows), `scopedRows.length ≤ limit` → `hasMore=false`, `nextCursor=null`, and a scoped manager saw "no more pages" while in-scope events still existed deeper in the table, with no continuation token — a truncated audit trail. Fixed by **loop-paging**: fetch keyset batches (advancing the composite `(createdAt,id)` cursor by the last RAW row each round) until `limit+1` IN-SCOPE rows are collected or the window is exhausted, then derive `hasMore`/`nextCursor` from the in-scope set. `MAX_SCAN_ROUNDS=25` bounds the worst case for a sparse-scope manager; on the cap the handler returns a partial page plus a cursor at the last raw row so the client resumes the scan instead of dropping deeper in-scope rows. Admin (`scope.ids===null`) keeps the single-round fast path, and the existing orderBy/cursor/`take=limit+1` shape-lock tests still pass unchanged. +2 regression tests covering the previously-UNTESTED RBAC-filtered branch (no truncation across batches + correct exhaustion). tsc 0; 32 audit tests green.

- **2026-06-03 (Fix — HeatMap freshness badge «Updated Xh ago» never rendered)** — Terminal bug-audit re-run (`we2d7o4h2`) P2 #7. `matrix/route.ts` had `computedAt: true` in the `select` for both the leaf `values` and the `parentValues` queries, but none of the three cell-building `.map()`s copied `computedAt` onto the emitted cell objects. - **2026-06-03 (Fix — operationalFact "snapshot" latest-by-date tie-break was non-deterministic)** — Terminal bug-audit re-run (`we2d7o4h2`) P3 #8. `listOperationalFacts` (`recompute-data-source.ts`) ran `findMany` with NO `orderBy`, and the snapshot branch of `operationalFactResolver` (`recompute-resolvers-a.ts`) reduced with strict `>` (`r.date > latest.date`). - **2026-06-03 (Fix — What-if scenarios showed spurious "improvements" on shock-unrelated indicators; the user's "BRENT oil-spike → wheat/grain cost improved")** — Terminal bug-audit #7 (P2). `simulateByDrivers` recomputed EVERY (company, indicator) pair with the shock overrides applied, then diffed the FRESH recompute against the STORED baseline `IndicatorValue`. - **2026-06-03 (Fix — EBITDA margin mixed raw-currency captured EBITDA with FX-converted revenue; latent)** — Terminal bug-audit re-run (`we2d7o4h2`) #4 (P2, latent). `budgetLineResolver` (`recompute-resolvers-b.ts`) preferred the source's own captured `pl_ebitda` operational-fact as the `IND_EBITDA_MARGIN` numerator, but `revenue` (the denominator) is FX-normalized to base currency by `aggregatePnlLines`, while `capture-plf-ebitda` stores `pl_ebitda` verbatim from the workbook cell with a hardcoded `unit`. - **2026-06-01 (Crisis sim — slow-hint + hard timeout so it never looks frozen)** — User: «не генерирует» (Run crisis stuck on "Modelling crisis…", no brief). Diagnosed via the dev log + a 3× timing probe: the `simulate?mode=drivers` call spiked to **55s** on one run, then measured **406/348/1350 ms** — a transient CPU-contention spike (many concurrent sessions on the machine), NOT a code bug or a value-190 blowup (the sim does fixed work regardless of shock magnitude). The real flaw was UX: `runDrivers` had no progress feedback or timeout, so a slow run read as frozen. Added: a "still computing… (high load)" hint after 8s (`crisis-slow-hint`) and a 90s `AbortController` hard timeout that surfaces a clear retry message (`crisisTimeout`) instead of hanging forever. Happy path re-verified live (brief still generates). +2 i18n keys ×3 locales. tsc 0; 49 ScenarioPanel tests. On-demand overlay → outside visual baseline.

- **2026-05-31 (Prod `migrate deploy` path VERIFIED end-to-end + a 2nd pg_dump-ism fixed — `migrate dev` had NOT surfaced it)** — Validated the baseline's headline benefit (clean fresh-DB deploys) by running the ACTUAL prod command against a throwaway DB: `DATABASE_URL=<fresh> prisma migrate deploy`. **Caught a real bug:** the init applied the full schema (60 tables + 56 RLS + 7 enums) but `migrate deploy` then failed **P1014** ("`_prisma_migrations` does not exist") — pg_dump emits `SELECT pg_catalog.set_config('search_path','',false)` which **empties the session search_path**, so after the init Prisma can't resolve its own unqualified `_prisma_migrations` bookkeeping table to record the migration. `migrate dev`'s shadow flow dodged this (different code path), so only testing the real prod command caught it — a first production deploy would otherwise have left a half-built, unrecorded schema. **Fix:** replaced that one line in the init with `SET search_path = public;` (keeps public in scope for both the init's object creation AND the post-init migration record). Re-synced the local real DB's recorded checksum (delete init row + `resolve --applied` → Prisma recomputes from the edited file; schema/data untouched). **Re-verified:** fresh-DB `migrate deploy` now applies cleanly ("All migrations have been successfully applied" — 60 tables / 56 RLS / 7 enums / 1 recorded), and real DB `migrate status` = "up to date". The full prod deploy path is now proven end-to-end on a throwaway fresh DB: provision → `migrate deploy` (60 tables / 56 RLS / 7 enums, recorded) → `seed-industries` (14) → `seed-indicators` (110 definitions) → ready for client-data import (companies=0 until import, as expected). Only the actual VM/secrets execution remains owner=user.

- **2026-05-31 (Prisma migration history REBASELINED — `migrate dev` unblocked; the earlier "RLS role lacks CREATEDB" diagnosis was WRONG)** — Investigated the `migrate dev` shadow-replay blocker end-to-end on user approval («да возьмись» → baseline). **Real root cause — NOT a CREATEDB/role issue (correcting the entry below):** the migration *history* was systemically incomplete. Multiple tables (`indicator_disclosures`, the ai_mapper/token/variance/predictive models, …) had been created via `prisma db push` and never captured in migration files, and one migration (`20260510210000`) FK-referenced a non-existent `"organizations"` table (real table is `"Organization"` — the model has no `@@map`). So the history could not replay from scratch (breaks `migrate dev` AND a fresh `migrate deploy`; existing DBs were fine only because their `_prisma_migrations` rows said *applied*). **Fix = baseline/squash:** generated ONE init migration from a `pg_dump --schema-only` of the REAL DB — deliberately NOT from `migrate diff`, because Prisma does not model the **56 RLS policies** (Phase 5.2) and a schema-only init would have silently dropped row-level security from every future deploy. Stripped pg_dump-16's `\restrict`/`\unrestrict` psql meta-commands (Prisma's engine runs SQL directly, not through psql). **Validated before any destructive step** by replaying the candidate init through Prisma's *actual* migration engine against a throwaway scratch DB (`migrate diff --from-migrations <init> --to-schema-datamodel --shadow-database-url <scratch>` → clean, exit 0). Placed as `prisma/migrations/00000000000000_init` (56 RLS policies, 60 tables, 7 enums, 2 fns, 2 triggers); archived the 111 broken migration dirs to `prisma/migrations_archive_pre_baseline_20260531/` (a sibling dir Prisma ignores); backed up `_prisma_migrations` (114 rows) then `DELETE` + `resolve --applied 00000000000000_init`. **Verified:** `migrate status` = "Database schema is up to date!"; `migrate dev` now shadow-replays the init cleanly (was the P3006/P1014 failure); the real DB schema/data/RLS are UNTOUCHED (`resolve` runs no DDL — re-checked live: RLS 56/56, companies 8, IVs 1194, intel 28). **Pre-existing drift surfaced (not hidden):** `migrate dev` cleanly generates a 5-statement reconciliation for 2 FKs where the DB is stricter than the committed schema (`cash_flow_entries.accountId` NOT NULL in DB vs `String?`+`SetNull` in schema; `balance_sheet_lines.companyId` onDelete) — left for a user product decision (CARRYOVER 2026-05-31), not auto-applied. **RESOLVED same day (user chose B — tighten schema→NOT NULL):** reconciled `schema.prisma` TO the DB (`CashFlowEntry.accountId String` + `onDelete: Restrict, onUpdate: Cascade`; `BalanceSheetLine.company onUpdate: NoAction`); `migrate dev` confirms **in-sync** (empty migration — DB was already NOT NULL, so zero DB change). `tsc` then surfaced the real cost of NOT NULL — 3 code paths create account-less `CashFlowEntry` rows — all fixed: (1) budget_line cash-flow generate now inherits `line.accountId` (BudgetLine.accountId is itself NOT NULL); (2) manual `POST /api/budgeting/cash-flow` now requires `accountId` (Zod; stale "FK still nullable at DB level" comment corrected) + a 400-contract test; (3) the invoice-derived generate path is DISABLED — an invoice has no single ChartOfAccount, and per the no-synthetic-data rule we won't fabricate one (the path was unused/0-rows + already try/catch-guarded; documented to re-enable with a real invoice→CoA mapping). Live data fully supports the constraint (309/309 cash-flow rows already carry an accountId). tsc 0; cash-flow tests 33; full suite 5459 (+1). The `BudgetLine(planId, deletedAt)` index (deferred behind this blocker below) is now addable via normal `migrate dev` (still gated PREMATURE at 8 cos).

(b) HeatMap virtualization is **scale-gated** on the same logic (3k cells matters at 60 cos, not 8) — deferred with the existing trigger. **Findings worth acting on later:** (1) the one justified index — `BudgetLine(planId, deletedAt)`, matching the dominant `{planId, deletedAt:null}` read shape across ~15 paths — was NOT added because **`prisma migrate dev` is currently blocked**: its shadow DB fails to replay migration `20260510210000…` ("`organizations` table does not exist") — almost certainly the restricted RLS `budgetpro_app` role lacks `CREATEDB` for the shadow DB. **Fix before any future `migrate dev`:** run migrations as `budgetpro_admin` (BYPASSRLS) or set `shadowDatabaseUrl` to an admin-owned DB. `migrate deploy` (prod) is unaffected (no shadow). (2) the FX-anchor freshness item was cosmetic (currency_rate_history 24 Apr vs cbar-official-fx 28 May — both 1.70, not even stale-flagged) → skipped as not worth churning 2 risk-class routes. **Net:** prevented 2 premature optimizations + 1 cosmetic change, delivered a real parallelization, and surfaced a migration-tooling blocker. The recompute resolver (`recompute-data-source.ts:312-327`), the Panel-3 drill-down (`indicators/values/[id]/drilldown`), and the 12-month series endpoint (`budget-lines/monthly-series`) ALL treat `sortOrder` — not `monthIndex` — as the 0..11 month index. 0`) — keeps all four readers consistent WITHOUT touching the core-calc bucketing logic; the sibling create paths (apply / apply-multi / budget / plans-clone / rolling / create-version) already set or preserved `sortOrder`, so `import-batch` was the sole buggy writer. **Live data repaired:** backfilled 545 live AzerSheker lines (`UPDATE sortOrder = monthIndex`) + recomputed via `recompute-fo-2026.ts` (6 companies, ok=105 / unknown=76 / failed=0). **DB-verified:** AZSEKER-CPC 2026-Q1 revenue (2,875,296) = exact sum of Jan(741,451)+Feb(959,158)+Mar(1,174,687); budget_lines now spread across `sortOrder` 0..3 with distinct per-month totals. **Containment confirmed:** the bug does NOT repeat in `balance_sheet_lines` / `cash_flow_entries` / `sales_budget_lines` / `cogs_budget_lines` — those store month in a dedicated `month Int NOT NULL` column (no defaultable field to silently collapse; DB shows sales 1..12, BS/CF 1..4 matching AzerSheker's 4-month coverage). 2 regression tests lock the writer invariant (`sortOrder == monthIndex`; null→0 fallback). tsc 0 throughout; affected suites green (import-batch 15/15). **Hardening (same day, follow-up commit):** the 3 month-readers (`recompute-data-source` / Panel-3 drill-down / 12-month series) now prefer `monthIndex` with a `sortOrder` fallback — coalesce-in-filter `OR: [{monthIndex: range}, {monthIndex: null, sortOrder: range}]` + `monthIndex ?? sortOrder` bucketing — matching the analytics/pnl readers, so month attribution no longer depends on the two columns staying synced (a future import path or hand-edit that mis-sets `sortOrder` can't silently re-collapse the months). **Proven no-op on current data:** re-recompute produced a byte-identical IV checksum (green 154/Σ340,467,085.74, red 55/Σ-23,189,206,868.22, amber 137/Σ1,494.94, unknown 452). 5 where-shape assertions repointed to the OR filter + 1 new row-resolution test (monthIndex wins; null→sortOrder; out-of-range→null); risk + drilldown + monthly-series suites 1784 green. *(Earlier punch-list #1-7 — plan-clone monthIndex, Panel-3 unit, board-deck weighting + cell-set — logged under 2026-05-29.)*

- **2026-05-29 (Phase 8 — board-deck visual-gate determinism fix; permanently-red gate → green-on-clean-code)** — Closed the board-deck sibling spec that the D1 closure flagged as red on clean code. Header doc rewritten to be honest about the new DOES/does-NOT-catch boundary (score block-position still locked; score micro-typography now unit-test territory, not pixel territory). Verified: HeroSection unit 16/16; regenerated baseline + 2 clean runs green (15.9s update, 6.2s verify); PNG visually confirmed — only the eyebrow `FO HOLDING` / `2026 · Review` renders as real text, every dynamic region is a solid mask band, zero score digits visible. The eyebrow year (`currentBakuYear()`) stays unmasked by choice — it rolls once a year (calendar event, not data-drift) and masking it would lose org-name/period alignment coverage; a 2027 baseline refresh is expected + trivial. `BASELINE UPDATE: board-deck-hero determinism — masked the composite score + caption (DATA-driven, recompute on every IndicatorValue change); this is NOT a layout change and NOT a data refresh — it stops the gate failing on score value churn while keeping all layout/frame/rhythm coverage.`

Helper `isMaterialityScoped(code)` gates the framework to the 5 ESG codes; financial/operational indicators are universally material so the matrix doesn't apply. **APIs:** `/api/indicators/matrix` builds per-(companyId, indicatorId) materiality at cell-emission time (pre-built lookup maps keep it O(1)); op-cells + real-rollup parent cells both carry the tag. `/api/indicators/values/[id]` adds `materiality` + `materialityNote` for the Panel-3 tooltip. **UI:** [HeatMap.tsx](src/features/terminal/components/HeatMap.tsx) — `low_materiality` → 0.45× base opacity (legible, status color preserved, drill-downable); `not_material` → 0.12× opacity + status color stripped to neutral gray `#1F2937` (effectively "this metric doesn't apply"). Cell `aria-label` extended with rating for screen readers. [IndicatorDetail.tsx](src/features/terminal/components/IndicatorDetail.tsx) — new `MaterialityBadge` component renders next to the provenance badge: amber-soft «НИЗКАЯ МАТЕРИАЛЬНОСТЬ» or neutral-gray «НЕ МАТЕРИАЛЬНО». `material` (default) + null (non-ESG) render nothing — adding "MATERIAL" on every cell would be visual noise. Tooltip surfaces SASB explanation + per-pair calibration note. **i18n:** 3 keys × 3 locales (`materiality.lowMateriality` / `notMaterial` / `tooltipSuffix`). **Tests:** new `esg-materiality.test.ts` (17 cases: canonical SASB calls — services × Scope 1 = not_material, industrial × Scope 1 = material; defensive defaults — null/unknown industry → material; note presence for non-default; gate scope = 5 ESG codes only) + `IndicatorDetail.test.tsx` extended (+4 cases: not_material badge + tooltip, low_materiality badge, material → no badge, null → no badge). Full vitest **3079 → 3100/3100** (+21); tsc 0. **End-to-end browser verify (preview :3003):** API correctly tags LLS-MAIN (services) × IND_CARBON_SCOPE_1 as `materiality: 'not_material'` and ATL-DBZ (industrial) × Scope 1 as `material`; HeatMap shows 59 material + 4 low_materiality + 2 not_material cells; Panel 3 on LLS-MAIN × Scope 1 displays **two stacked badges** (ОТРАСЛЕВАЯ ОЦЕНКА B + НЕ МАТЕРИАЛЬНО) with full tooltip "SASB-материальность: показатель не приоритетен для этой отрасли. No direct combustion / production heat. Scope 1 effectively zero." **F4 family complete:** клиент теперь видит на каждой ESG-ячейке (1) откуда цифра берётся [v2.1], (2) насколько модель достоверна [v2.2.1], (3) можно ли её исправить ручным вводом [v2.3], (4) важна ли вообще эта метрика для этого сектора [v2.4]. - **2026-04-23** — Phase 7.A.0 ✅ Formula engine:
  - `src/lib/risk/formula-engine.ts` — pure sync engine built on `expr-eval` (sandboxed: no assignment, no `in`, no factorial, no concatenation).
  - Two entry points: `tryEvaluateFormula(...)` returns `{ ok: true, value } | { ok: false, code, reason }` (batch recompute uses this — one broken indicator must not abort the tenant's run); `evaluateFormula(...)` is the throwing wrapper for scenario UI preview / dev tooling. Error codes: `'parse' | 'eval' | 'non_finite'`.
  - `FormulaContext` narrowed to `Record<string, number>` (non-number context values would coerce to NaN silently — literals like `"rooms_sold"` belong as function args, not context vars). `FormulaFunctionArg` = `number | string` documents the looser function-call boundary.
  - Threshold classifier `classifyValue(value, thresholds)` — direction-agnostic, first matching band wins green→amber→red. Supports `between` bands.
  - `validateThresholds(thresholds, direction)` — write-time guard for seed/API input. Catches the silent-miscast trap (e.g. `higher_better` with `green.value < amber.value`), between bands with lo ≥ hi, non-finite band values, and forbids `between` in green/amber for `higher_better`/`lower_better` directions (between + classify collapses the "tighter band wins first" invariant — use between only with `band` direction). Recompute stays direction-agnostic; validation runs on definition write, not read.
  - `src/lib/risk/formula-engine.test.ts` — 32 vitest tests. Engine: arithmetic, variables, ternaries, custom functions (incl. nested), parse/eval errors, `1/0`+`0/0` → `non_finite`, JS globals + constructor-chain escapes (`(0).constructor.constructor(...)`) all blocked, huge exponents (`10^400`) surface as `non_finite` not silent Infinity, deep nesting (30 levels) survives, unicode identifiers either resolve or fail cleanly. Classifier: green-first ordering, `lower_better` flip, `between` bands, NaN/Infinity → unknown, no-match → unknown. `validateThresholds`: accepts correct higher/lower_better, rejects inverted bands, rejects lo ≥ hi, rejects non-finite values, skips direction check for `band` direction.
  - `vitest.config.ts` — node env, `@/` path alias to `src/`, test glob `src/**/*.test.ts`.
  - `package.json` — added `"test": "vitest run"` and `"test:watch": "vitest"`; `expr-eval` in deps, `vitest` in devDeps.
  - Verified: `npx vitest run` → 34/34 pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean on engine + tests.
  - Not in this task: recompute pipeline (next — needs background queue), `fact`/`rollup` resolvers against Prisma (will live in the pipeline, not the engine). Recompute will use `tryEvaluateFormula` + map `{ ok: false }` → `IndicatorValue { status: 'unknown', inputs: { error: reason } }` for drill-down.
- **2026-04-23** — Phase 7.A.0 ✅ Recompute pipeline:
  - `src/lib/risk/periods.ts` + 18 tests — period string (`YYYY-MM` / `YYYY-Qn` / `YYYY`) → UTC half-open range `[start, end)` + `daysInPeriod` + `expandToMonths`. Rejects unpadded / out-of-range / garbage input with typed `PeriodParseError`.
  - `src/lib/risk/recompute.ts`:
    - Narrow `RecomputeDataSource` interface — `listBookings`, `listOperationalFacts`, `getCompanySettings`, `upsertIndicatorValue`. Every method takes `organizationId` explicitly, so tenant scoping is enforced at the DS layer (not optional).
    - Thin `createPrismaDataSource(prisma)` adapter maps to the Phase-7 Prisma models with `where: { organizationId, ... }` on every read. A recompute call with mismatched `organizationId` + `companyId` simply gets empty rows — no cross-tenant leak into the computed value.
    - `buildContext` uses a `NamespaceResolver` registry pattern (`bookingResolver`, `companySettingsResolver`, `operationalFactResolver`) + a post-processing step for cross-namespace derivations (`rooms_available`). Each resolver is run at most once per recompute even when multiple inputs hit its namespace (e.g. `"booking"` + `"booking.sourceCountry"`). Adding a new namespace = implement one `NamespaceResolver`, no surgery on the builder.
    - Booking resolver now tracks `missing_rate_count` — non-null currency without `exchangeRate` would otherwise silently fall back to rate=1 and hide FX data-quality problems behind a green indicator.
    - Inputs snapshot has a flat typed shape — `{ resolved, aggregates, derived, error? }` with snake_case keys throughout. `aggregates` is typed per namespace (`BookingAggregate`, `OperationalFactAggregate`, `CompanySettingsAggregate`) so drill-down UI reads typed properties, not `any`; `derived` likewise typed (`rooms_available?` for now). `resolved` mirrors the formula context; `error` present only on failure.

Matches the architect-frozen engine contract.

  - **Critical flaw discovered before AAC import:** the prior `upsertBudgetLine` (findFirst + update/create on `(planId,companyId,accountId,category)`) was idempotent on **identical** input but left **stale rows** when the source Excel was edited. Postgres ACID guarantees: parse failure mid-way rolls back the delete automatically — file either fully lands or pre-existing state is untouched. Helpers reshaped: `ensureChartOfAccountTx(tx, ...)` / `insertBudgetLineTx(tx, ...)` take the transaction client.

NOT applied to `parseSummaryRollupSheet` because synthetic codes (`ROLLUP-REVENUE`, `ROLLUP-REVENUE-OTHER`, `ROLLUP-OPEX-GA`) use dashes as semantic separators — `ROLLUP-REVENUE` and `ROLLUP-REVENUE-OTHER` are siblings, not parent/child.

- **2026-04-24** — Phase A — **Reconciliation guard (finance-safety fix-before-build)** — architect round-2 flagged silent data loss in the parent-rollup dedup above: dropping a parent unconditionally assumed `sum(children) = parent.plannedAnnual`, so any delta from unallocated / catchall amounts would vanish without a trace. Finance-unacceptable:
  - **Fix — `src/lib/onboarding/adapters/azmade-sopl.ts`.** `dedupeParentRollups` now reconciles every identified parent against the **sum of its topmost descendants** (not direct children — sparse hierarchies like `721 + 721-02-01` without intermediate `721-02` would otherwise mis-count). Topmost-descendants = codes whose dash-segment ancestor walk hits the parent without passing through any other in-set code. Tolerance = `max(1, |parent| × 0.01)` (1 AZN OR 1%, whichever is larger — covers AZN cents rounding and small Excel edits).
    - |delta| ≤ tol → safe drop (parent fully absorbed by children).
    - |delta| > tol → inject synthetic `<parent>-__UNALLOCATED__` leaf carrying `parent.plannedAnnual − Σchildren`, with per-month delta computed in the same basis. Label = `<parent label> (unallocated)`. Total preserved, no double-count. `__UNALLOCATED__` sentinel is unambiguous vs. real SAP codes (double-underscore + uppercase).
  - **New `ParseResult.parentRollupsUnallocated`** field surfaces every synthetic injection (code, parentCode, plannedAnnual) so finance sees a clear audit trail. `scripts/import-azmade-budgets.ts` adds `⚠ reconciliation: N parent(s) exceeded sum of children; injected __UNALLOCATED__ leaves for delta. e.g. <code>→<value>` at warning level per job.
  - **Tests — 6 new** (196/196 total): delta = 0 within tolerance (safe drop), delta > tol (positive synthetic), delta < -tol (negative synthetic for children-over-parent), rounding-band boundary (0.005 stays dropped), non-dash suffixes (`721A`, `72102` NOT treated as children of `721` — dash-hierarchy invariant), sparse hierarchy (`721 + 721-02-01` with missing `721-02` reconciles against the leaf).
  - **Real finance deltas caught on re-import (which would have been silently lost):**
    - AAC-MAIN `601-01` (main revenue bucket) — parent stated 17,233,219 AZN but sum of its topmost descendants was 610,500 lower. Delta preserved as `601-01-__UNALLOCATED__`.
    - AAC-MAIN `711-10` — 4,800 AZN delta, preserved.
    - LLS-MAIN `721-11` (Amortization) — 38,618 AZN delta, preserved (matches the ~0.5% discrepancy seen in the earlier LLS inspection — now surfaced rather than absorbed).
  - **DB state after reconciliation:** 568 `BudgetLine` rows (+3 over prior 565 = exactly the 3 synthetic unallocated leaves injected). `ChartOfAccount` rows 293 → 296 (new synthetic codes cataloged). `Recompute done: ok=40 unknown=0 failed=0` — ratio integrity preserved because synthetic rows keep the same `accountType` as their dropped parent, so `budgetLine` resolver's revenue/cogs/opex sums remain invariant.
  - **Idempotency re-verified:** immediate second run reports `inserted=568 deleted=568` (same state). Architect round-3: **PASS**. `+3 row audit` closed — every added row is a reconciliation-guard injection accounted for in the warning log.
  - Tolerance is a starting default (1% / 1 unit). Tighten to 0.5% if the 60-company load shows it firing too rarely. Architect-noted non-blocking.

- **2026-06-03 (Fix — board-deck export buttons showed RAW i18n keys to the client; wrong namespace)** — Post-audit E2E triage caught a real client-facing bug: `ExportPdfButton`, `ExportPptxButton`, and `PrintButton` all used `useTranslations("boardDeck.exports")`, but the board-deck i18n lives under `terminal.boardDeck.exports` (every board-deck server component uses `getTranslations("terminal")`; the root-level `boardDeck` is only the sidebar nav-label string). The namespace missed → next-intl returned the raw key paths, so the export buttons rendered literal `pdfLabel` / `pptxLabel` / `printLabel` (and broken aria-labels `pdfAriaLabel` etc.) to users. It went unnoticed because the board-deck-v2 smoke spec's PPTX assertion used a loose `/pptx/i` regex that matched even the raw key `pptxAriaLabel`; only the anchored `/^export board snapshot to pdf$/i` PDF assertion exposed it. Fixed all three to `terminal.boardDeck.exports`. `board-deck-v2` E2E went from a 27.6s timeout-fail to a 2.9s pass; 181 board-deck unit tests still green (they mock `useTranslations`, so the namespace bug was invisible at the unit layer — only the real-messages E2E caught it). tsc 0. (Separately flagged in CARRYOVER: the board-deck HERO visual baseline drifted −234px/13% — a pre-existing hero layout/data change, unrelated to this fix, pending a visual look before any baseline regen.)
- **2026-06-03 (Fix — restored `npm run lint` under Next 16 / eslint flat config)** — Next 16 removed the `next lint` command, so the `lint` script just errored "Invalid project directory: .../lint" (lint had been dead the whole Next-16 era). Restored it: `lint` script → `eslint .`; new `eslint.config.mjs` flat config built on the canonical `eslint-config-next` (core-web-vitals + typescript + next plugin). Two real eslint-version incompatibilities had to be resolved: (1) the project was on eslint ^10.2.0, but eslint-config-next@16's bundled `eslint-plugin-react`/`react-hooks` call eslint-9 APIs removed in eslint 10 (`context.getFilename`, `scopeManager.addGlobals`) and crash — pinned eslint to ^9 (nothing depended on 10 since lint was broken); (2) pinned `settings.react.version="19"` to skip eslint-plugin-react's eslint-version-sensitive React-version auto-detection. Added ignores for `**/.next/**` (any depth) + `.claude/**` so eslint stops crawling sibling git-worktree build artifacts. The codebase ran for a long time with NO lint, so eslint-config-next's strictest rules flag a 161-item pre-existing backlog; those (the new react-compiler hooks lints — set-state-in-effect ×55, purity, static-components, immutability — plus exhaustive-deps and react/no-unescaped-entities) are dialled to **warn** so `npm run lint` is GREEN + usable now, by injecting the override into next's own config objects (the only place the plugins are in scope under flat config). `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` is KEPT at error as a real-bug guard; the single known-safe violation (CommodityTickerPanel calling useQuery once per static REGION) carries a justified inline disable. `npm run lint` now exits 0 (0 errors / 161 warnings); tsc 0. The `verify-ebitda` E2E (EDEN-green / CPC-red) now passes. **Caveat surfaced for the user:** 2026 is a PARTIAL year (only 3-4 months booked) so EDEN's 169.8% margin (437K EBITDA on 257K revenue) is a partial-year artefact, not a steady-state figure (2025 full year = 5.6M rev / 1.56M EBITDA / 28% — sane); whether 2026 should be shown as-is is a data-completeness call. **Two follow-ups (tracked in CARRYOVER):** (1) the prod DB needs the same `capture-plf-ebitda` re-run (this fix was applied to the dev DB); (2) a pipeline gap — the AzerSheker AI import clears operational_facts on re-import without re-capturing the EBITDA subtotal, so this will recur on the next re-import unless `capture-plf-ebitda` is wired into the import apply-step (or `pl_ebitda` is preserved).

Two commits, one conceptual change each (handoff §6). **`src/lib/risk/period-context.ts`** — the §4.1 contract with every field carried and none dropped, plus `buildPeriodContext()`, which takes the facts it needs as inputs rather than fetching them (`computedAt` is injected, never `Date.now()`), so it is deterministic and DB-free. The load-bearing pair is `coverageMonths` vs `expectedCoverageMonths` — the structural form of two real defects from the 2026-07-15 FO-workbook session: a month of revenue booked to the previous year by a 24s LMT drift, and an EBITDA margin reading 169.8% "green" off ~4 booked months of a 12-month year. Both were period-context failures: the number was right, the claim about *which period it spoke for* was not. So `2026` holding 5 months is partial while `2026-YTD-05` holding the same 5 is complete — §4.2's "Actual through May is YTD May, not FY Actual". Key grammar reuses the strings already on `IndicatorValue.period` for MONTH/QUARTER/FY (so the contract describes existing data with **no migration**); YTD/LTM had no stored form and get `YYYY-YTD-MM` / `YYYY-LTM-MM`, still matching the `^\d{4}` probe `isPartialYear` relies on. LTM is reported under its **ending** year. Date math delegates to `periods.ts` and stays UTC half-open; `timeZone` is a declaration of the fiscal calendar's zone, **not** an instruction to shift timestamps — conflating those is exactly what produced the 24s drift. `hasFullCoverage()` is named narrowly on purpose: it is only §4.3's coverage clause, **not** the completeness gate (which also needs structural tests, reconciliation, a lock and an identifiable revision — none of which exist). **`src/lib/risk/data-revision.ts`** — §5.1's fields incl. the six reason codes verbatim, and §5.2's rules as pure predicates: `requiresNewRevision()`, `correctionReasonFor()` (a locked period yields `late_adjustment`, never an in-place edit of an approved snapshot) and `isCurrent()` (superseding never deletes). `computeRevisionContentHash()` is SHA-256 over canonical JSON, matching `src/lib/budgeting/period-snapshot.ts` so the codebase keeps **one** hashing convention; id lists hash as **sets** (sorted + de-duplicated) so a re-import pulling the same artifacts in another order does not spawn a phantom revision; identity/lifecycle fields are excluded because if approving a revision changed its hash, the hash could no longer answer "is this the same source state?". **Deliberately no Prisma model:** persisting revisions is additive schema work and every sibling table carries RLS policies — adding one without them risks the cross-org exposure 05 §13 lists as an immediate rollback trigger, so it gets its own reviewed slice. **Zero runtime change: both modules are unimported by design.** No financial formula, threshold, KPI or value touched. 71 new tests (38 + 33), incl.
