- **2026-07-16 (Phase 10 / B5 — the first import-revision writer; blanket observation stamping withdrawn after review)** — The import-side revision becomes recorded: the single-sheet staging apply route (`/api/onboarding/import/staging/[id]/apply`) now calls `ensureDataRevision()` **inside the transaction that commits the import**, but does not pass that workbook-only revision into the generic recompute. New `src/lib/risk/import-lineage.ts` derives the ids from what was actually imported — `sourceArtifactIds: ['import-staging:<cuid>']` (the staging row, deliberately **not** the filename: two unrelated workbooks are both `budget.xlsx`, and a filename-keyed revision would hand the second import the first one's lineage) and `mappingVersionIds: ['effective-mapping:<sha256>']` over the semantic mapping actually applied — column `role`, `currencyCode` and account-type overrides, excluding the mapper's `confidence`/`reasoning` prose so a reworded LLM explanation cannot spawn a phantom revision. Not the approved-template version: that record is written post-commit and best-effort, so reading it at apply time would name a version the import did not necessarily use. **The boundary, stated exactly:** apply ↔ revision **is** atomic (one transaction — a failed import leaves no revision claiming it happened, and a failed revision write takes the import down with it, both tested against the real `$transaction` callback). Revision ↔ IndicatorValue is **not**, because recompute is post-commit on *every* import path in this codebase (`apply:687`, `apply-multi:878`, `apply-multi-entity:655`, `budget:323`, each with its own comment explaining that recompute cannot fit the interactive tx) — and per `03-DATA-KPI-TRUST-SPEC` §6.1/§6.4 it is not supposed to be: a source mutation emits a downstream event; the current batch recompute intentionally carries no workbook-only revision until each indicator complete dependency set can be proven. The task's request for three-way atomicity is therefore not achievable without restructuring the canonical import path, which handoff §2.8 forbids; `indicatorsStale` already reports the gap. **An independent adversarial review found three real defects in the first cut, all fixed here, and the first was the serious one:** (1) **Provisional was being lifted.** `use-heat-map-model.ts` passes `requireLineage: true`, and its justification comment was stale — it reasoned from `lastReconciledAt`, which commit `a8c5b7fa` had already replaced with `revisionId` as the lineage signal. So stamping a revision would have certified every freshly imported cell as decision-grade: never reconciled, never coverage-checked, never methodology-approved. `decision-grade.ts` gained the `no_reconciliation` rule its own comment already claimed to enforce ("both are required"), and the surface now requires it. 0 of 1,269 rows carry `lastReconciledAt`, so the badge verdict — and the rendered matrix — are unchanged. (2) **Lineage would have started lying.** `upsertIndicatorValue` preserved `revisionId` when the caller passed `undefined`, modelled on the sparkline rule. The analogy is wrong: a sparkline is independent data another writer owns, but a `revisionId` is a property of the `value` written on the same line. The nightly cron, which threads no revision, would have overwritten value/status/computedAt and left the import's revision attached to a number it never produced — a wrong pointer reads as evidence where `null` reads as its absence. Lineage is now written on every update, so presence means "this revision produced this number", never "some revision once did"; the live-DB test that asserted the old behaviour is inverted, with the reasoning kept. (3) **Parent rollups were over-stamped.** The trigger fans out to *every* level-1 company in the org, so importing one child would have stamped every holding's rollup with a revision naming one child and one workbook. The batch now leaves both leaf observations and parent rollups untraced until a revision can speak for every input of one observation. Also closed from the review: `currencyCode` added to the mapping hash (it picks which amount column wins and tags `BudgetLine.currencyCode` — it changes the money). **Zero financial change, measured not asserted:** 1,269 IVs / 0 traced / 0 reconciled / 0 revisions / 498 coloured / ΣIV 413,796,007.3851349 / ΣBudgetLine 1,062,640,716.182965 — identical before and after; no backfill, and the writer is inert until a real import runs. - **2026-07-16 (Phase 10 / B2 — DataRevision persistence: additive table + RLS + DB-enforced immutability)** — Closes the half of B2 that was deferred. `prisma/migrations/20260716052925_data_revision/` is **additive only** — every statement targets the new table; `indicator_values` count is 1,269 before and after; applied locally with Prisma 6.19.3 (`migrate dev`, no reset, no drift). **Isolation ships in the same migration as the table**, so `data_revisions` never exists without it: `tenant_isolation` copied verbatim from the baseline pattern (`20260706183514_rls_trade_tables`). Unset `app.organization_id` → `current_setting` returns NULL → `"organizationId" = NULL` is NULL, not TRUE → **deny by default**; `FOR ALL` with no explicit `WITH CHECK` means USING governs writes, so a cross-org INSERT is rejected by the same expression. **Immutability is enforced by a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger, not convention** — the pinned source state (org, scope, reason, contentHash, createdAt) cannot be UPDATEd; only `lockedAt`/`reconciledAt`/`approvedAt` move, because §5.1 requires the revision to carry that state. `createdById`/`supersedesId` needed a narrower rule than "never changes": both are `ON DELETE SET NULL`, which Postgres implements as an **UPDATE**, so a blanket ban would have made deleting a User fail outright — they may go to NULL but never to a different value (provenance can be forgotten when its subject is deleted, never rewritten to point elsewhere). - **2026-08-01 (11.86 — the AI import records where its numbers came from; code-tested, not deployed)** — Production carried 6,460 indicator values and 0 lineage rows because the lineage writer was wired into three staging routes the client never uses, and because no route in the codebase attached a revision to an observation at all. The live AI multi-file import now hashes each uploaded workbook's bytes, builds a `DataRevision` from the committed groups' own write results after they commit, and passes it to the recompute, which stamps it **per (company × indicator × period)** only where `IndicatorDefinition.requiredInputs` is entirely workbook data the run wrote clean-slate under an `actual` plan. Measured on production: 252 of 1,428 coloured cells qualify — 10 of the 56 on the terminal's default 2025 matrix; the rest read a market feed, a rollup, a manual fact or a constant and stay honestly untraced. Reconciliation is deliberately left unstamped — the import's db-readback verdict is about `budget_line` rows, not about derived values — with the run↔revision join recorded in the audit event instead. Two writer-level invariants were hardened at the same time: shadow-only `external_refresh` revisions are refused, and an update now invalidates a stale reconciliation stamp the way it has always invalidated a stale revision pointer. No schema change (`prisma migrate diff` against `postgres:16`: no difference). The Risk Terminal's LEGACY banner is unchanged, correctly: the reconciliation axis is still unmet, and `/api/indicators/matrix` still never emits `computedAt`, so every coloured cell also trips the fail-closed `stale` rule on the wire.
